Subsection.Text: In addition to the information specified in subsection (1), the Chief Electoral Officer may invite the member to provide other information that the Chief Electoral Officer considers necessary to implement agreements made under section 55, but the member is not required to provide that information.

The original of a statement of ordinary residence of an elector, other than a statement completed under section 195, shall be sent to the Chief Electoral Officer and a copy of that original shall be kept in the unit in which the elector is serving.
On receiving the statement of ordinary residence, the Chief Electoral Officer shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: validate it by indicating on it the name of the electoral district that includes the place of ordinary residence shown in the statement; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: return it to the commanding officer of the unit in which the elector is serving.

Subsection.Text: On receiving the statement of ordinary residence, the commanding officer shall destroy the copy kept under subsection (1) and keep the validated original with the elector's unit service documents.

On receiving the validated statement of ordinary residence, the commanding officer may destroy any other original or copy of a statement of ordinary residence that was filed with the elector's unit service documents.

Section.Text: A statement of ordinary residence completed by a member of the reserve force of the Canadian Forces under section 195 shall be filed with the unit in which the member is on full-time training or service or active service, as the case may be.
Statements of ordinary residence shall be retained for a period of one year after a person ceases to be entitled to vote under this Division and may be destroyed at the end of that period.
Subsection 199(2) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: The coordinating officer shall, on request, provide to the Chief Electoral Officer the following information relating to each elector or future elector:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: his or her surname, given names, gender, rank and service number;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: his or her date of birth;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the civic address and mailing address of his or her place of ordinary residence; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: his or her current mailing address.

Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer may use the information provided under subsection (2) to update the Register of Electors or Register of Future Electors.

The Chief Electoral Officer may retain the information provided under subsection (2), but not included in the Register of Electors or Register of Future Electors, for the purpose of correlating information subsequently collected with information already contained in the relevant register.

The Chief Electoral Officer may provide the coordinating officer with the information referred to in paragraphs (2)(a) to (d) relating to each elector or future elector who has provided a service number under this Part.
The coordinating officer shall, on request, provide to the Chief Electoral Officer the following information relating to each elector:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the elector's surname, given names, sex and rank;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the elector's date of birth;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the civic address of the elector's place of ordinary residence indicated on any validated statement of ordinary residence; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the elector's current mailing address.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 199:
The coordinating officer shall cooperate with the special voting rules administrator to facilitate the voting, under Divisions 3 and 4 of this Part, of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a person employed by or in support of the Canadian Forces outside Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a person who accompanies a unit or other element of the Canadian Forces that is on service or active service outside Canada, within the meaning of subsection 61(1) of the National Defence Act; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a person who resides outside Canada with a member of the Canadian Forces or with a person referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

Subsection.Text: The Minister of National Defence shall designate one or more electors as liaison officers to work, during and between election periods, with the Chief Electoral Officer and the coordinating officer in carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Division.
The coordinating officer shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the name and address of each liaison officer as each one is designated.

Section.Text: Sections 200 to 203 of the Act are replaced by the following:
Without delay after the issue of the writs, the Chief Electoral Officer shall inform the Minister of National Defence and the coordinating officer of their issue.
On being informed of the issue of the writs, the coordinating officer shall inform each liaison officer and commanding officer of their issue.

On being informed of the issue of the writs, a liaison officer shall give each commanding officer in respect of whose unit the liaison officer has liaison duties all necessary information for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Division.

Without delay after the issue of the writs, the Chief Electoral Officer shall inform the Minister of National Defence and the coordinating officer of their issue and of the location of voting territories and administrative centres.
On being informed of the issue of the writs, the Minister of National Defence shall designate one or more electors to act as liaison officers for the vote.
On being informed of the issue of the writs, the coordinating officer shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: inform each commanding officer of their issue; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: inform the Chief Electoral Officer of the name and address of each liaison officer.

Subsection.Text: On being designated, a liaison officer shall communicate with each commanding officer in respect of whose unit the liaison officer has liaison duties, with respect to any matter that relates to the vote.
A liaison officer shall cooperate with the Chief Electoral Officer in the administration of the vote.
Paragraph 204(2)(b) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the commanding officer will designate one or more unit election officers to collect their votes and fix the voting times during the voting period.

Subsection.Text: The notice shall notify electors that an election has been called and of the date of polling day and shall inform the electors that

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the commanding officer will designate one or more deputy returning officers to collect their votes and fix the voting times during the voting period.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 204(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

The list shall be arranged alphabetically and shall indicate each elector's surname, given names and service number, the address of his or her place of ordinary residence and his or her electoral district.
The list shall be arranged alphabetically and shall indicate each elector's surname, given names, sex and rank, and

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the elector's statement of ordinary residence has been validated, the name of the elector's electoral district; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the elector's statement of ordinary residence has not been validated, the place of ordinary residence as indicated in the statement of ordinary residence.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 204:

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of maintaining operational security, a commanding officer may indicate on the list of electors, with respect to some or all of the electors in the commanding officer's unit, their alternative address rather than the address that would otherwise be indicated under subsection 204(3).

For the purpose of maintaining operational security or out of a reasonable apprehension of bodily harm if the address of his or her place of ordinary residence were to appear on the list of electors, an elector may ask his or her commanding officer not to indicate that address on the list of electors. The commanding officer, unless he or she considers that it would not be in the public interest to do so, shall grant the request and indicate the elector's alternative address on the list.
The commanding officer shall inform the special voting rules administrator, through a liaison officer, that an alternative address has been indicated under this section.
For greater certainty, the indication of an alternative address on the list of electors under this section does not change the elector's place of ordinary residence for the purposes of this Act.
The portion of subsection 205(1) of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:
After being informed of the issue of the writs, but no later than the 28th day before polling day, each commanding officer shall
Within seven days after being informed of the issue of the writs, each commanding officer shall

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: designate an elector as the deputy returning officer for each polling station;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: through a liaison officer, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a list of the designated deputy returning officers and their ranks, and sufficient copies of the list of electors for the unit; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: provide the designated deputy returning officers with a copy of the list of electors for the unit.

Subsection.Text: Paragraphs 205(1)(b) to (d) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: designate a sufficient number of electors as unit election officers to allow for voting to take place at each polling station;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: through a liaison officer, provide the special voting rules administrator with a list of the unit election officers and their ranks, and the list of electors for the unit; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: provide the unit election officers with the list of electors for the unit.

Section.Text: Section 207 of the Act is replaced by the following:

The commanding officers of units may establish a joint polling station for electors in their units, if the commanding officers consider that it would be useful to do so for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Division.

The commanding officers of units that are in the same locality may establish one polling station for all electors in their units, if the commanding officers consider that it would be expedient for the purposes of this Division.
Paragraphs 209(a) and (b) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: distribute the materials to the unit election officers; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: display the list in one or more conspicuous places or make it otherwise accessible to electors in their unit.

Section.Text: On receiving election materials and the list of candidates, each commanding officer shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: distribute the materials in sufficient quantities to the designated deputy returning officers; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: post copies of the list in conspicuous places.

Section.Text: Sections 210 to 212 of the Act are replaced by the following:
During the voting period, a unit election officer shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: display the voting instructions provided by the Chief Electoral Officer in relation to the vote under this Division in conspicuous places at each polling station or make them otherwise accessible to electors; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: keep available for consultation by the electors the text of this Part, the election materials necessary for determining in which electoral district an elector is entitled to vote and the list of candidates.

Section.Text: A Canadian citizen may represent a registered party at a polling station if he or she provides the unit election officer with a copy of an authorization in the prescribed form signed by a candidate for the party.

Subsection.Text: Each elector, on arriving at the polling station, shall give his or her name and service number and the address of his or her place of ordinary residence to the unit election officer and, on request, to a representative of a registered party.
For the purpose of subsection (1), if an alternative address is indicated on the list of electors under section 204.1 in respect of the elector, the elector may provide that alternative address.

If the unit election officer determines that the elector's name, service number and address appear on the list of electors, then the elector shall provide the officer with the following proof of the elector's identity:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: one piece of identification issued by the Canadian Forces that contains a photograph of the elector and his or her name and service number; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: two pieces of identification of a type authorized under section 211.3 each of which establishes the elector's name and at least one of which establishes his or her service number.

Subsection.Text: A representative of a registered party may examine, but not handle, any piece of identification presented under this section.
If the unit election officer is satisfied that an elector's identity has been proven in accordance with this section, the elector's name shall be crossed off the list of electors.

Section.MarginalNote: Application for registration and special ballot

Subsection.Text: An elector whose name does not appear on the list of electors or whose address on the list does not correspond with the elector's place of ordinary residence may complete an application for registration and special ballot and provide the unit election officer with the following proof of the elector's identity:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: one piece of identification issued by the Canadian Forces that contains a photograph of the elector and his or her name and service number; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: two pieces of identification of a type authorized under section 211.3 each of which establishes the elector's name and at least one of which establishes his or her service number.

Subsection.Text: An application for registration and special ballot shall be in the prescribed form and shall include the following information relating to each elector:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: his or her surname and given names;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: his or her date of birth;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: his or her service number;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the civic address and mailing address of his or her place of ordinary residence;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: his or her current mailing address; and

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: any other information that the Chief Electoral Officer considers necessary to determine the electoral district in which he or she is entitled to vote.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of maintaining operational security or out of a reasonable apprehension of bodily harm if he or she were to indicate the addresses referred to in paragraph 2(d), the elector may apply to the elector's commanding officer to use another address for that purpose. The commanding officer, unless he or she considers that it would not be in the public interest to do so, shall grant the application and provide the elector with the alternative address that is to be used on the application for registration and special ballot.

In addition to the information specified in subsection (2), the Chief Electoral Officer may request that the elector provide other information that the Chief Electoral Officer considers necessary for implementing agreements made under section 55, but the elector is not required to provide that information.
A representative of a registered party may examine, but not handle, any piece of identification presented under this section.

If the unit election officer is satisfied that an elector's identity has been proven in accordance with this section, the unit election officer shall accept the application for registration and special ballot.
If an alternative address is used in accordance with subsection (3), subsections 204.1(3) and (4) apply with any necessary modifications.

Section.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer may authorize types of identification, in consultation with the coordinating officer, for the purposes of paragraphs 211.1(3)(b) and 211.2(1)(b). For greater certainty, any document may be authorized, regardless of who issued it.

The unit election officer shall require the elector whose name has been crossed off the list of electors or whose application for registration and special ballot has been accepted to sign the declaration prescribed by the Chief Electoral Officer.
During the voting period, a deputy returning officer for a unit shall, at each polling station,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: put in conspicuous places two or more copies of voting instructions provided by the Chief Electoral Officer and relating to the vote under this Division in the prescribed form; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: keep available for consultation by the electors one copy of this Part, one set of street indexes, one guide to electoral districts and one list of candidates.

Section.Text: A Canadian citizen may represent a registered party at a polling station if he or she provides the deputy returning officer with an authorization in the prescribed form signed by a candidate for the party.

Before delivering a special ballot to an elector, a deputy returning officer shall require the elector to complete a statement of ordinary residence, if none has been placed in the elector's unit service documents, and to make and sign the declaration on the outer envelope.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 213(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

A unit election officer shall, once the elector has signed the declaration referred to in section 212, give the elector a special ballot, an inner envelope, the declaration — if it is not on the outer envelope — and the outer envelope.
An elector who has received a special ballot under subsection (1) may vote only under this Division.
A deputy returning officer shall, on completion of the documents referred to in section 212, give the elector a special ballot, an inner envelope and the outer envelope signed by the elector.
The portion of subsection 213(2) of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:
The elector shall use the special ballot to vote by writing on it, in private, the name of the candidate of his or her choice, folding it and, in the presence of the unit election officer,

The elector shall use the special ballot to vote by writing on it, in private, the name of the candidate of his or her choice, folding the special ballot and, in the presence of the deputy returning officer,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: placing the inner envelope in the outer envelope and sealing the outer envelope.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 213(2)(b) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: placing the inner envelope and the declaration — if it is not on the outer envelope — in the outer envelope and sealing the outer envelope.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 213(4) of the Act is replaced by the following:
If the special ballot is incapable of being used, the elector shall return it to the unit election officer, who shall mark it as a spoiled ballot and give the elector another special ballot.

If an elector has inadvertently handled a special ballot in such a manner that it cannot be used, the elector shall return it to the deputy returning officer who shall mark it as spoiled and give an additional special ballot to the elector.
Subsection 214(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Information to be provided to elector

Subsection.Text: The unit election officer shall inform an elector that, in order for the special ballot to be counted, the outer envelope must be received by the special voting rules administrator in the National Capital Region no later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day. The unit election officer shall inform the elector of the service provided by the Canadian Forces to deliver the outer envelope.

The deputy returning officer shall inform an elector that, in order to be counted, the outer envelope must be received by the special voting rules administrator in Ottawa not later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day. The deputy returning officer shall inform the elector of the location of the nearest post office or mail box and of the service provided by the Canadian Forces to deliver the outer envelope.
Subsection 214(3) of the Act is repealed.
If the elector chooses to use a postal service, the deputy returning officer must ensure that sufficient postage is affixed to the outer envelope.

Section.Text: Section 215 of the Act is replaced by the following:
A unit election officer who is qualified to vote may vote in accordance with this Division.
A deputy returning officer who is qualified to vote may vote in accordance with this Division.

Subsection.Text: The portion of subsection 216(1) of the Act before paragraph (b) is replaced by the following:
If an elector is unable to read or because of a disability is unable to vote in the manner described in this Division, the unit election officer shall assist him or her by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: completing the declaration referred to in section 212 and writing the elector's name where the elector's signature is to be written; and

Subsection.Text: If an elector is, because of a physical disability, unable to vote in the manner described in this Division, the deputy returning officer shall assist him or her by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: completing the declaration on the outer envelope and writing the elector's name where his or her signature is to be written; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: marking the special ballot as directed by the elector in his or her presence and in the presence of another elector selected by the elector as a witness.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 216(1)(b) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: marking the special ballot as directed by the elector in the elector's presence and in the presence of another elector selected by the elector as a witness.

Subsection.Text: The portion of subsection 216(2) of the Act before paragraph (b) is replaced by the following:
The unit election officer and an elector acting as a witness shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sign a note on the declaration indicating that the elector was assisted; and

Subsection.Text: The deputy returning officer and an elector acting as a witness shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sign a note on the outer envelope indicating that the elector was assisted; and

Section.Text: Subsections 217(2) and (3) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Subsection.MarginalNote: Unit election officer for hospitalized electors
Subsection.Text: If no unit election officer has been designated for a service hospital or convalescent institution, the unit election officer for the unit to which the hospital or institution belongs is the unit election officer for electors who are patients in the hospital or institution.

A unit election officer for electors who are patients in a service hospital or convalescent institution may, if that officer considers it advisable and the officer in charge of the hospital or institution approves, go from room to room to administer and collect the votes of electors who are confined to bed.

If no deputy returning officer has been designated for a service hospital or convalescent institution, the deputy returning officer for the unit to which the hospital or institution belongs is the deputy returning officer for electors who are patients in the hospital or institution.

A deputy returning officer for electors who are patients in a service hospital or convalescent institution may, if that officer considers it advisable and the commanding officer for the unit approves, go from room to room to administer and collect the votes of electors who are confined to bed.

Section.Text: Sections 218 and 219 of the Act are replaced by the following:

An elector who provides satisfactory evidence of his or her absence from his or her unit during the voting times fixed for the polling stations in that unit because of duty, leave or furlough may apply to a unit election officer of another unit, in accordance with section 211.2, to vote at that officer's polling station.

Section.MarginalNote: Delivery of documents to the commanding officer

Subsection.Text: The unit election officer shall deliver to the unit's commanding officer,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: at the end of each voting day, if feasible, and no later than the end of the voting period, the outer envelopes containing the marked special ballots, the applications for registration and special ballot that were accepted by the unit election officer and the service number of each elector who received a special ballot; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: at the end of the voting period, any spoiled outer envelopes, any spoiled special ballots and any other election documents and election materials in the unit election officer's possession.

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the outer envelopes and applications for registration and special ballot referred to in paragraph (1)(a), the commanding officer shall deliver them to the special voting rules administrator.

On receipt of the service numbers referred to in paragraph (1)(a), the commanding officer shall inform the special voting rules administrator, through the liaison officer, of the identity of the electors who received a special ballot.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Delivery of election documents and election materials
Subsection.Text: On receipt of the election documents and election materials referred to in paragraph (1)(b), the commanding officer shall deliver them to the special voting rules administrator with all other election documents and election materials in the commanding officer's possession.

On being informed under subsection 219(1.2) that an elector has received a special ballot, the special voting rules administrator shall inform the returning officer for the electoral district of the elector's place of ordinary residence of this.
When the returning officer is informed under subsection (1) that an elector has received a special ballot, he or she shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the elector's name is not already included on a list of electors, enter the elector's name on the list of electors for the appropriate polling division in that electoral district; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: indicate on the list of electors that the elector has received a special ballot.

Section.Text: An elector who provides satisfactory evidence of their absence from their unit during the voting times fixed for the polling stations in his or her unit because of duty, leave or furlough may apply to a deputy returning officer of another unit to vote at that officer's polling station.

Subsection.Text: At the end of the voting period, the deputy returning officer for a unit shall deliver to the unit's commanding officer

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the outer envelopes that contain the marked special ballots;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any unused or spoiled outer envelopes;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: any unused or spoiled special ballots and unused inner envelopes; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: in a separate and clearly identified parcel, every statement of ordinary residence completed at the time of voting.

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the documents referred to in subsection (1), the commanding officer shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: deal with the originals and copies of the statements of ordinary residence in accordance with this Division; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: deliver to the Chief Electoral Officer all other documents and election materials received from the deputy returning officers.

Section.Text: The heading of Division 3 of Part 11 of the Act is replaced by the following:
The definitions elector and register in section 220 of the Act are replaced by the following:

Definition.Text: elector means an elector who resides outside Canada. (électeur)
register means the register referred to in section 222. (registre)
elector means an elector, other than a Canadian Forces elector, who resides temporarily outside Canada. (électeur)
register means the register referred to in subsection 222(1). (registre)

Section.Text: Sections 221 and 222 of the Act are replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Inclusion in register of electors resident outside Canada
Section.Text: An elector may vote under this Division if

Paragraph.Text: his or her application for registration and special ballot is received by the special voting rules administrator in the National Capital Region no later than 6:00 p.m. on the 6th day before polling day; and
his or her name is entered on the register.

Section.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer shall maintain a register of electors in which is entered the surname, given names, gender, date of birth, civic address, mailing address and electoral district of each elector who has filed an application for registration and special ballot in order to vote under this Division and who, at any time before making the application, resided in Canada.

An elector may vote under this Division if his or her application for registration and special ballot is received in Ottawa by 6:00 p.m. on the 6th day before polling day and his or her name is entered on the register.

Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer shall maintain a register of electors who are temporarily resident outside Canada in which is entered the name, date of birth, civic and mailing addresses, sex and electoral district of each elector who has filed an application for registration and special ballot and who

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: at any time before making the application, resided in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: has been residing outside Canada for less than five consecutive years immediately before making the application; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: intends to return to Canada to resume residence in the future.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph (1)(b) does not apply to an elector who is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: employed outside Canada in the federal public administration or the public service of a province;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: employed outside Canada by an international organization of which Canada is a member and to which Canada contributes;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a person who lives with an elector referred to in paragraph (a) or (b); or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a person who lives with a member of the Canadian Forces or with a person referred to in paragraph 191(d).

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 223(1)(b) of the Act is repealed.
An application for registration and special ballot may be made by an elector. It shall be in the prescribed form and shall include

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if paragraph 222(1)(b) does not apply in respect of the elector, proof of the applicability of an exception set out in subsection 222(2);

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the date the elector left Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the address of the elector's last place of ordinary residence in Canada before he or she left Canada or the address of the place of ordinary residence in Canada of the spouse, the common-law partner or a relative of the elector, a relative of the elector's spouse or common-law partner, a person in relation to whom the elector is a dependant or a person with whom the elector would live but for his or her residing temporarily outside Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: the date on which the elector intends to resume residence in Canada;

Subsection.Text: Paragraphs 223(1)(d) to (f) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the address of the elector's place of ordinary residence;

Section.Text: Section 226 of the Act is amended by adding "or" at the end of paragraph (d), by striking out "or" at the end of paragraph (e) and by repealing paragraph (f).
The Chief Electoral Officer shall delete from the register the name of an elector who

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: except for an elector to whom any of paragraphs 222(2)(a) to (d) applies, has resided outside Canada for five consecutive years or more.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 227(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

After approving an application for registration and special ballot and after the issue of the writs, the Chief Electoral Officer shall provide a special ballot to every elector whose name is entered in the register.

After approving an application for registration and special ballot and after the issue of the writs, the Chief Electoral Officer shall send a special ballot, an inner envelope and an outer envelope to every elector whose name is entered in the register, at the address referred to in paragraph 223(1)(g).
Paragraph 227(2)(b) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: placing the ballot in an inner envelope and sealing it;

Subsection.Text: An elector shall vote by special ballot by

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: placing the ballot in the inner envelope and sealing it;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: placing the inner envelope in the outer envelope; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: signing the declaration on the outer envelope and sealing it.

Subsection.Text: Paragraphs 227(2)(c) and (d) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: signing the declaration prescribed by the Chief Electoral Officer; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: placing the inner envelope and the declaration — if it is not on the outer envelope — in the outer envelope and sealing it.

Section.Text: Section 229 of the Act is replaced by the following:
The special ballot must be received by the special voting rules administrator in the National Capital Region no later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day in order to be counted.
The special ballot must arrive at the office of the Chief Electoral Officer in Ottawa not later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day in order to be counted.
Sections 231 and 232 of the Act are replaced by the following:
For the purpose of this Division, elector means an elector, other than an incarcerated elector, who resides in Canada and who wishes to vote in accordance with this Division.

Section.MarginalNote: Conditions for voting by special ballot

Subsection.Text: An elector may vote under this Division if his or her application for registration and special ballot is received by a returning officer in an electoral district or by the special voting rules administrator after the issue of the writs but before 6:00 p.m. on the 6th day before polling day.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Conditions for voting by special ballot — specified later day
Subsection.Text: If, for the purpose of this subsection, the Chief Electoral Officer specifies on his or her Internet site a day that is after the 6th day before polling day but before polling day, an elector may vote under this Division if his or her application for registration and special ballot is received by the returning officer in the elector's electoral district or by the special voting rules administrator after the issue of the writs but before 6:00 p.m. on the specified day.

The Chief Electoral Officer may specify a day for the purpose of subsection (2) only if he or she considers that the integrity of the vote will not be affected if applications for registration and special ballots are received after 6:00 p.m. on the 6th day before polling day.

Section.Text: For the purpose of this Division, elector means an elector, other than a Canadian Forces elector or an incarcerated elector, who resides in Canada and who wishes to vote in accordance with this Division.
An elector may vote under this Division if his or her application for registration and special ballot is received after the issue of the writs and before 6:00 p.m. on the 6th day before polling day

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: by a returning officer in an electoral district; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: by the special voting rules administrator.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 233(1)(a) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the elector's name and the address of his or her place of ordinary residence;

Subsection.Text: The application for registration and special ballot shall be in the prescribed form and shall include the following information:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the elector's name and place of ordinary residence;

Subsection.Text: Subsection 233(1.1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

An elector who would be under reasonable apprehension of bodily harm if he or she were to indicate the address of his or her place of ordinary residence or his or her mailing address for the purpose of paragraph (1)(a) or (d) may apply to the returning officer or special voting rules administrator to use another address for that purpose. The returning officer or special voting rules administrator, unless he or she considers that it would not be in the public interest to do so, shall grant the application and shall not reveal the addresses in respect of which the application is made except as required to send the special ballot to the elector. For greater certainty, the granting of the application does not change the elector's place of ordinary residence for the purposes of this Act.

An elector who would be under reasonable apprehension of bodily harm if he or she were to indicate the mailing address of his or her dwelling place for the purpose of paragraph (1)(d) may apply to the returning officer or special voting rules administrator to use another address for that purpose. The returning officer or special voting rules administrator, unless he or she considers that it would not be in the public interest to do so, shall grant the application and shall not reveal that other address except as required to send the special ballot to the elector. For greater certainty, the granting of the application does not change the elector's place of ordinary residence for the purposes of this Act.
Subsection 233(3) of the Act is repealed.
An elector who makes an application for registration and special ballot shall indicate whether his or her name is already on a list of electors.

Section.Text: Section 234 of the Act is repealed.

Subsection.Text: The special voting rules administrator shall inform the returning officer of any elector whose name is on a list of electors for the returning officer's electoral district and who has received a special ballot from another electoral district. The returning officer shall indicate on the list of electors that the elector has received a special ballot.

If an elector's name is not already included on a list of electors, the special voting rules administrator shall so inform the returning officer for the electoral district in which the elector is to vote by special ballot. The returning officer shall enter the elector's name on the list of electors for the appropriate polling division in that electoral district and shall indicate that the elector has received a special ballot.

Section.Text: Sections 236 and 237 of the Act are replaced by the following:

Once an elector's application for registration and special ballot has been accepted by the returning officer or special voting rules administrator, he or she shall ensure, in accordance with the Chief Election Officer's instructions,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that the elector's name is entered on the list of electors for the polling division of the elector's place of ordinary residence, if it is not already included on a list of electors; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: that there is an indication on the list of electors that the elector has received a special ballot.

Subsection.Text: Subject to subsection (2) and section 237.1, on acceptance of an elector's application for registration and special ballot, the elector shall be provided with a special ballot.
If section 241 applies, then, on acceptance of an elector's application for registration and special ballot, the elector shall be given a ballot, an inner envelope and an outer envelope.

Section.Text: If an elector applies for registration and special ballot in his or her electoral district, the returning officer shall, if necessary, add the elector's name to the appropriate list of electors and shall indicate on the list that the elector has received a ballot in accordance with this Division.

Subject to section 237.1, on acceptance of an elector's application for registration and special ballot, the elector shall be given a special ballot, or, if section 241 applies, a ballot, an inner envelope and an outer envelope.

Subsection.Text: Subsections 237.1(3.1) and (3.2) of the Act are repealed.
No elector shall attest to the residence of more than one elector at an election.
No elector whose own residence has been attested to at an election shall attest to another elector's residence at that election.
Paragraph 237.1(4)(b) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (d.2)

Section.Text: Sections 238 and 239 of the Act are replaced by the following:
An elector who has been provided with a special ballot may vote only by following the procedure set out in subsections 227(2) and (3).

Section.MarginalNote: Receipt of special ballot — application made outside electoral district

Subsection.Text: In order to have their special ballot counted, an elector whose application for registration and special ballot was accepted by the special voting rules administrator or by a returning officer outside the elector's electoral district shall ensure that the special ballot is received by the special voting rules administrator in the National Capital Region no later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day. The special ballot shall be transmitted by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sending the sealed outer envelope to the special voting rules administrator by mail or any other means; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: delivering it to a Canadian Embassy, High Commission or Consular Office, to a Canadian Forces base outside Canada or to any other place that the Chief Electoral Officer designates.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Receipt of special ballot — application made in electoral district
Subsection.Text: In order to have their special ballot counted, an elector whose application for registration and special ballot was accepted by the returning officer in the elector's electoral district shall ensure that the ballot is received at the office of that returning officer before the close of the polling stations on polling day.

Despite subsection (2), a special ballot referred to in that subsection that is received by the special voting rules administrator in the National Capital Region no later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day shall be counted.

Section.Text: An elector who has received a special ballot may vote in accordance with subsections 227(2) and (3).

Subsection.Text: An elector who does not vote in his or her electoral district shall send the sealed outer envelope to the special voting rules administrator

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: by mail or any other means; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: by delivering it to a Canadian Embassy, High Commission or Consular Office, to a Canadian Forces base outside Canada or to any place that the Chief Electoral Officer may designate.

Subsection.Text: In order to have the special ballot counted, an elector shall ensure that the ballot is received

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the special ballot is cast in the elector's electoral district, at the office of the returning officer before the close of the polling stations on polling day; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the special ballot is cast outside the elector's electoral district, at the office of the special voting rules administrator in Ottawa, not later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 242(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

If the ballot or special ballot is incapable of being used, the elector shall return it to the election officer, who shall mark it as a spoiled ballot and give the elector another ballot or special ballot.

If an elector has inadvertently handled a ballot or a special ballot in such a manner that it cannot be used, the elector shall return it to the election officer who shall mark it as a spoiled ballot and give the elector another ballot.
An elector shall not be given more than one ballot under subsection (1).
Subsection 242(2) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:
An elector shall not be given more than one ballot or special ballot, as the case may be, under subsection (1).
The portion of subsection 243(1) of the Act before paragraph (b) is replaced by the following:

When an elector personally goes to the office of the returning officer and is unable to read or because of a disability is unable to vote in the manner described in this Division, the designated election officer shall assist the elector by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: completing the declaration referred to in paragraph 227(2)(c) and writing the elector's name where the elector's signature is to be written; and

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: completing the declaration on the outer envelope and writing the elector's name where his or her signature is to be written; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: marking the ballot as directed by the elector in his or her presence.

Paragraph 243(1)(b) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)

Subsection.Text: Subsection 243(2) of the Act is replaced by the following:
An election officer who assists an elector under subsection (1) shall indicate, by signing the note on the declaration, that the elector was assisted.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 243:

Section.MarginalNote: Assistance by friend or related person

Subsection.Text: If an elector requires assistance to vote, one of the following persons may accompany the elector into the voting compartment at the office of the returning officer and assist the elector to mark his or her ballot:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a friend of the elector;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the elector's spouse or common-law partner; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a relative of the elector or of the elector's spouse or common-law partner.

Subsection.Text: A person described in subsection (1) who wishes to assist an elector in marking a ballot shall first make a solemn declaration in the prescribed form that he or she

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: will mark the ballot paper in the manner directed by the elector;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: will not disclose the name of the candidate for whom the elector voted;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: will not try to influence the elector in choosing a candidate; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: has not, during the current election, assisted another person, as a friend, to mark a ballot.

Subsection.Text: The portion of subsection 243.1(1) of the Act before paragraph (b) is replaced by the following:

On application of an elector who is unable to read — or who is unable to vote in the manner described in this Division because of a disability — and who is unable to personally go to the office of the returning officer because of a disability, an election officer shall go to the elector's dwelling place and, in the presence of a witness who is chosen by the elector, assist the elector by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: completing the declaration referred to in paragraph 227(2)(c) and writing the elector's name where the elector's signature is to be written; and

Subsection.Text: On application of an elector who is unable to read, or who is unable to vote in the manner described in this Division because of a physical disability, and who is unable to personally go to the office of the returning officer because of a physical disability, the designated election officer shall go to the elector's dwelling place and, in the presence of a witness who is chosen by the elector, assist the elector by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: completing the declaration on the outer envelope and writing the elector's name where the elector's signature is to be written; and

The election officer and the witness who assist an elector under subsection (1) shall indicate, by signing the note on the declaration, that the elector was assisted.
The election officer and the witness who assist an elector under subsection (1) shall indicate, by signing the note on the outer envelope, that the elector was assisted.

Section.Text: Section 246 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Before the 10th day before polling day, each liaison officer shall ensure that an application for registration and special ballot in the prescribed form is completed for every eligible elector of the correctional institution who wishes to vote, indicating his or her place of ordinary residence as determined under subsection (2).

Subsection.MarginalNote: Procedure when elector votes more than once
Subsection.Text: If, after receiving an elector's outer envelope but before counting the inner envelopes, the special ballot officers ascertain that the elector has voted more than once, they shall set the elector's inner envelope aside unopened.

If, after receiving but before counting the outer envelopes, the special ballot officers ascertain that an elector has voted more than once, they shall lay the outer envelopes that relate to the elector aside unopened.

Subsection.Text: When an inner envelope is set aside unopened as described in subsection (1) or (2),

Subsection.Text: Subsection 267(4) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.Text: Sections 273 and 274 of the Act are replaced by the following:

The returning officer shall, as soon as possible, notify the candidates of the names of the election officers who he or she assigns to verify the declarations referred to in paragraph 227(2)(c) and to count the special ballots issued to electors in his or her electoral district and received at his or her office.

A candidate or his or her representative may be present for the verification of the declarations referred to in paragraph 227(2)(c) and the counting of ballots received at the returning officer's office.

Subsection.Text: The returning officer shall appoint a deputy returning officer and poll clerk to verify the outer envelopes and to count the special ballots issued to electors in his or her electoral district and received in his or her office. More than one deputy returning officer and poll clerk may be appointed if the number of votes warrants it.

The returning officer shall assign duties so that a deputy returning officer chosen from among the persons recommended by the registered party whose candidate finished first in the last election in the electoral district works with a poll clerk chosen from among the persons recommended by the registered party whose candidate finished second in that election in that electoral district.

For the purpose of subsection (2), in determining whether the candidate of a registered party finished first or second in the last election in a case where the registered party is the result of a merger with one or more parties that were registered parties at the last election, there shall be attributed to the candidate of the merged party, the number of votes of the candidate of the merging party with the largest number of votes at that last election.
The returning officer shall, as soon as possible, notify the candidates of the name and address of the persons appointed as the deputy returning officer and the poll clerk.

Section.Text: A candidate or his or her representative may be present for the verification of the outer envelopes and the counting of ballots received at the office of the returning officer.

Subsection.Text: One of the election officers shall be provided with the applications for registration and special ballot received before the deadline, along with any other materials that may be required.
The deputy returning officer shall be provided with the applications for registration and special ballot received before the deadline, along with any other materials that may be required.
The portion of subsection 277(1) of the Act before paragraph (d) is replaced by the following:
An election officer referred to in section 273 shall set aside an elector's inner envelope unopened if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the information concerning the elector, as set out in the elector's declaration made under paragraph 227(2)(c), does not correspond with the information on the application for registration and special ballot;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the declaration — other than one in respect of an elector who has voted with assistance under section 243 or 243.1 — does not bear the elector's signature;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the elector has voted more than once; or

Subsection.Text: The deputy returning officer shall set aside an outer envelope unopened when he or she ascertains on its examination that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the information concerning the elector, as described on the outer envelope, does not correspond with the information on the application for registration and special ballot;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the outer envelope, other than an outer envelope in respect of an elector who has taken a vote under section 243 or 243.1, does not bear the signature of an elector;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: more than one ballot has been issued to an elector; or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the outer envelope was received after the prescribed deadline.

Subsection.Text: When the outer envelopes are verified, the poll clerk shall register any objection to an elector's right to vote in the electoral district in the prescribed form.

When an outer envelope is set aside unopened as described in subsection (1), the deputy returning officer shall note on it the reasons for the rejection. The deputy returning officer and the poll clerk shall initial the envelope.
Paragraph 277(1)(d) of the French version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: d)
Paragraph.Text: l'enveloppe extérieure est reçue après le délai fixé.

Subsection.Text: Subsections 277(2) and (3) of the Act are replaced by the following:
When the declarations are verified, an election officer referred to in section 273 shall register any objection to an elector's right to vote in the electoral district in the prescribed form.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Noting of reasons for setting aside
Subsection.Text: When an elector's inner envelope is set aside unopened as described in subsection (1), the election officer who set it aside shall note on it the reasons for the setting aside. The election officer and another election officer referred to in section 273 shall both initial the envelope.
When an elector's inner envelope is set aside unopened as described in this section, it shall be kept with the outer envelope and — if it did not appear on the outer envelope — the declaration.

Section.Text: Section 278 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: The election officers referred to in section 273 shall count all inner envelopes that have not been set aside.
They shall put all the inner envelopes that have not been set aside in a ballot box provided by the returning officer.

After the close of the polling stations, one of the election officers shall open the ballot box and, together with another of the election officers, shall open the inner envelopes and count the votes.
The deputy returning officer and the poll clerk shall count all valid outer envelopes.
The deputy returning officer and the poll clerk shall open the outer envelopes and put all the inner envelopes in a ballot box provided by the returning officer.
After the close of the polling stations, the deputy returning officer shall open the ballot box and he or she together with the poll clerk shall open the inner envelopes and count the votes.
The portion of subsection 279(1) of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:
An election officer shall, in counting the ballots, reject a ballot if
The deputy returning officer shall, in counting the ballots, reject a ballot if
Subsections 279(2) and (3) of the Act are replaced by the following:
An election officer shall not reject a special ballot for the sole reason that the elector has incorrectly written the name of a candidate, if the ballot clearly indicates the elector's intent.

An election officer shall not reject a special ballot for the sole reason that the elector has written, in addition to the name of a candidate, the candidate's political affiliation, if the ballot clearly indicates the elector's intent.

The deputy returning officer shall not reject a special ballot for the sole reason that the elector has incorrectly written the name of a candidate, if the ballot clearly indicates the elector's intent.

The deputy returning officer shall not reject a special ballot for the sole reason that the elector has written, in addition to the name of a candidate, the candidate's political affiliation, if the ballot clearly indicates the elector's intent.

Section.Text: The headings before section 281 and sections 281 and 282 of the Act are replaced by the following:
The provisions of this Part apply inside and outside Canada.
The Chief Electoral Officer shall not vote at an election.

Section.MarginalNote: Inducing Chief Electoral Officer to vote
Section.Text: No person shall induce or attempt to induce the Chief Electoral Officer to vote at an election knowing that it is the Chief Electoral Officer whom he or she is inducing or attempting to induce to vote and that the Chief Electoral Officer is prohibited from voting.
No person shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: vote or attempt to vote at an election knowing that he or she

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is not a Canadian citizen — or will not be a Canadian citizen — on polling day, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: is not 18 years of age or older — or will not be 18 years of age or older — on polling day; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: induce or attempt to induce another person to vote at an election knowing that the other person

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is not a Canadian citizen — or will not be a Canadian citizen — on polling day, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: is not 18 years of age or older — or will not be 18 years of age or older — on polling day.

Section.MarginalNote: Not ordinarily resident in electoral district
Section.Text: No person shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: vote or attempt to vote at an election in a particular electoral district knowing that his or her place of ordinary residence is not in that electoral district; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: induce or attempt to induce another person to vote at an election in a particular electoral district knowing that the other person's place of ordinary residence is not in that electoral district.

Section.MarginalNote: Voting more than once — general election

Subsection.Text: No person who has voted in a general election shall vote again, or attempt to vote again, in that general election.
No person who has voted in a by-election shall vote again, or attempt to vote again, at that by-election or at any other by-election that is held on the same day.
Every person present at a polling station or at the counting of the votes shall maintain the secrecy of the vote.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Attempting to obtain information about elector's vote
Subsection.Text: Except as provided by this Act, no person shall, in a polling station, attempt to obtain any information as to the candidate for whom any elector is about to vote or has voted.
Except as provided by this Act, no person shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: on entering the polling station and before receiving a ballot or special ballot, openly declare for whom he or she intends to vote;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: while in the polling station, show his or her ballot or special ballot, when marked, so as to allow the name of the candidate for whom he or she has voted to be seen; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: before leaving the polling station, openly declare for whom he or she has voted.

Subsection.Text: No person who has seen a ballot or special ballot that has been marked by an elector shall disclose information as to how it was marked unless he or she is the elector who marked it or he or she has been authorized to make the disclosure by the elector who marked it.

No person shall, at the counting of the votes, attempt to obtain information or communicate information obtained at the counting as to the candidate for whom a vote is given in a particular ballot or special ballot.
No person shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: request or apply for a ballot or special ballot in a name that is not his or her own;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: vote using a forged ballot or forged special ballot;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: request or apply for a ballot or special ballot to which he or she is not entitled;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: provide a ballot or special ballot to any person when not authorized under this Act to do so;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: have a ballot or special ballot in his or her possession when not authorized under this Act to do so;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: alter, deface or destroy a ballot or the initials of the election officer that are signed on a ballot;

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: put or cause to be put into a ballot box a ballot, special ballot or other paper otherwise than as provided by this Act or by instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer;

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: take a ballot out of the polling station or the office of the returning officer otherwise than as provided by this Act or by instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer; or

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: destroy, take, open or otherwise interfere with a ballot box or book or packet of ballots or special ballots otherwise than as provided by this Act or by instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer.

Subsection.Text: No election officer shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: with the intent of causing the reception of a vote that should not have been cast or the non-reception of a vote that should have been cast, put his or her initials on the back of any paper purporting to be or capable of being used as a ballot at an election; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: place on a ballot or special ballot any writing, number or mark with intent that the elector to whom the ballot or special ballot is to be given, or has been given, can be identified.

Subsection.Text: No unit election officer shall place on a special ballot any writing, number or mark with intent that the elector to whom the special ballot is to be given, or has been given, can be identified.

Section.MarginalNote: Photograph, video or copy of marked ballot

Subsection.Text: No person shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: take a photograph or make a video recording of a ballot or special ballot that has been marked, at an election, by an elector;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: make a copy, in any manner, of any ballot or special ballot that has been marked, at an election, by an elector; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: distribute or show, in any manner, to one or more persons, a photograph, video recording or copy of a ballot or special ballot that has been marked, at an election, by an elector.

Subsection.Text: Subsection (1) does not apply to any person with a visual impairment who takes a photograph or makes a video recording or copy of a ballot or special ballot that he or she has marked for the purpose of verifying the accuracy of their marking.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who does anything referred to in that subsection for the purpose of a recount under Part 14 or for the purpose of any other legal proceeding.

Section.Text: No person shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: make a false statement in an application for registration and special ballot; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: make a false statement in a declaration signed by him or her before an election officer or unit election officer.

Subsection.Text: At an election, no person shall, as a friend, assist under section 155 or 243.01, more than one elector for the purpose of marking a ballot.
No person who assists an elector under section 155 or 243.01 shall, directly or indirectly, disclose the name of the candidate for whom the elector voted or that candidate's political affiliation.

Section.MarginalNote: Vouching for more than one person

Subsection.Text: No person shall vouch for more than one person at an election.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Voucher not qualified as elector, etc.
Subsection.Text: No person shall vouch for another person if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the person who vouches is not qualified as an elector;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the person who vouches does not personally know the other person; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the person who vouches does not reside in the same polling division as the other person.

Subsection.Text: No person who has been vouched for at an election shall vouch for another person at that election.

Section.Text: No person shall, in a polling station or in any place where voting at an election is taking place, influence or attempt to influence electors to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the election.

Section.MarginalNote: Influencing electors — election officers and staff of returning officers
Section.Text: Subject to section 141, no election officer, unit election officer or member of the staff of a returning officer shall, while exercising their powers or performing their duties, influence or attempt to influence an elector to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at an election.

Subsection.Text: No person or entity referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (e) shall, during an election period, unduly influence an elector to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the election:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: an individual who is not a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and who does not reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a corporation or entity incorporated, formed or otherwise organized outside Canada that does not carry on business in Canada or whose only activity carried on in Canada during an election period consists of doing anything to influence electors during that period to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the election;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a trade union that does not hold bargaining rights for employees in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a foreign political party; or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: a foreign government or an agent or mandatary of a foreign government.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subsection (1), a person or entity unduly influences an elector to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at an election if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: they knowingly incur any expense to directly promote or oppose a candidate in that election, a registered party that has endorsed a candidate in that election or the leader of such a registered party;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: they knowingly make or publish a false statement that is prohibited under paragraph 91(1)(a) or (b) in respect of a candidate in that election, a registered party that has endorsed a candidate in that election or the leader of such a registered party; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: one of the things done by them to influence the elector is an offence under an Act of Parliament or a regulation made under any such Act, or under an Act of the legislature of a province or a regulation made under any such Act.

Subsection.Text: For greater certainty, subsection (1) does not apply if the only thing done by the person or entity to influence the elector to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for the particular candidate or registered party, consists of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: an expression of their opinion about the outcome or desired outcome of the election;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a statement by them that encourages the elector to vote or refrain from voting for any candidate or registered party in the election; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the transmission to the public through broadcasting, or through electronic or print media, of an editorial, a debate, a speech, an interview, a column, a letter, a commentary or news, regardless of the expense incurred in doing so, if no contravention of subsection 330(1) or (2) is involved in the transmission.

Subsection.Text: No person or entity shall act in collusion with a person or entity to whom subsection (1) applies for the purpose of contravening that subsection.

No person or entity shall sell any advertising space to a person or entity to whom subsection (1) applies for the purpose of enabling that person or entity to unduly influence an elector to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at an election within the meaning of this section.

Section.Text: No person shall interfere with, or attempt to interfere with, an elector who is marking a ballot or special ballot.
No person shall prevent or attempt to prevent an elector from voting at an election.

Subsection.Text: No person shall, during an election period, directly or indirectly, offer a bribe to influence an elector to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the election.

No person shall, during an election period, accept or agree to accept a bribe that is offered to them to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the election.

Section.Text: No person shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: by intimidation or duress, compel or attempt to compel a person to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at an election; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: by any pretence or contrivance, including by representing that the ballot or special ballot or the manner of voting at an election is not secret, influence or attempt to influence a person to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at an election.

ExplanatoryNote.Label: Clause 190:
ExplanatoryNote.ExplanatoryText: Existing text of the heading and sections 281 and 282:

Section.Text: No person shall, inside or outside Canada,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: wilfully disclose information as to how a ballot or special ballot has been marked by an elector;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: wilfully interfere with, or attempt to interfere with, an elector when marking a ballot or special ballot, or otherwise attempt to obtain any information as to the candidate for whom any elector is about to vote or has voted;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: knowingly make a false statement in an application for registration and special ballot;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: knowingly apply for a ballot or special ballot to which that person is not entitled;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: knowingly make a false statement in a declaration signed by him or her before a deputy returning officer;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: knowingly make a false declaration in the statement of ordinary residence completed by him or her;

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: wilfully prevent or endeavour to prevent an elector from voting at an election; or

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: wilfully at the counting of the votes, attempt to obtain information or communicate information obtained at the counting as to the candidate for whom a vote is given in a particular ballot or special ballot.

Section.Text: No person shall, outside Canada,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: by intimidation or duress, compel a person to vote or refrain from voting or vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate at an election under this Part; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: by any pretence or contrivance, including by representing that the ballot or the manner of voting at an election is not secret, induce a person to vote or refrain from voting or vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate at an election under this Part.

Subsection.Text: Subsections 283(1) and (2) of the Act are replaced by the following:
Immediately after the close of a polling station, an election officer who is assigned to the polling station shall count the votes in the presence of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: another election officer who is assigned to the polling station; and
any candidates or their representatives who are present or, if no candidates or representatives are present, at least two electors.

Subsection.Text: One of those election officers shall supply all the persons referred to in paragraph (1)(b) who are present and who request one with a tally sheet to keep their own score of the voting.

Immediately after the close of a polling station, the deputy returning officer shall count the votes in the presence of the poll clerk, any person appointed under section 32.1 whose duties include being present at the count and any candidates or their representatives who are present or, if no candidates or representatives are present, at least two electors.
The deputy returning officer shall supply the poll clerk and all the persons referred to in subsection (1) who are present and who so request with a tally sheet to keep their own score of the voting.
The portion of subsection 283(3) of the Act before paragraph (b) is replaced by the following:
The election officer who counts the votes shall, in the following order,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: count the number of electors who voted, count the number of those to whom a certificate was given under subsection 161(4), make an entry at the end of the list of electors that states "The number of electors who voted at this election is (stating the number). Of these, the number of electors to whom a certificate was given under subsection 161(4) is (stating the number).", sign the list and place the list in the envelope supplied for that purpose;

Subsection.Text: The deputy returning officer shall, in the following order,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: count the number of electors who voted at the polling station, count the number of those to whom a certificate was given under subsection 161(4), make an entry at the end of the list of electors that states "The number of electors who voted at this election in this polling station is (stating the number). Of these, the number of electors to whom a certificate was given under subsection 161(4) is (stating the number).", sign the list and place the list in the envelope supplied for that purpose;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: total the number of electors indicated under paragraph (a) who voted at the polling station and the numbers arrived at in paragraphs (b) and (c) in order to ascertain that all ballots that were provided by the returning officer are accounted for;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: examine each ballot, show the ballot to each person who is present, and ask the poll clerk to make a note on the tally sheet beside the name of the candidate for whom the vote was cast for the purpose of arriving at the total number of votes cast for each candidate.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 283(3)(d) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: total the number of electors indicated under paragraph (a) who voted and the numbers arrived at in paragraphs (b) and (c) in order to ascertain that all ballots that were provided by the returning officer are accounted for;

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 283(3)(f) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: examine each ballot, show the ballot to each person who is present, and ask the election officer referred to in paragraph (1)(a) to make a note on the tally sheet beside the name of the candidate for whom the vote was cast for the purpose of arriving at the total number of votes cast for each candidate.

Subsection.Text: The portion of subsection 284(1) of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:
In examining the ballots, the election officer who counts the votes shall reject one
In examining the ballots, the deputy returning officer shall reject one
Subsections 284(2) and (3) of the Act are replaced by the following:
No ballot shall be rejected by reason only that an election officer placed on it any writing, number or mark, or failed to remove the counterfoil.

If a ballot is found with the counterfoil attached, the election officer who counts the votes shall, while concealing the number on it from all persons present and without examining it, remove and destroy the counterfoil.
No ballot shall be rejected by reason only that the deputy returning officer placed on it any writing, number or mark, or failed to remove the counterfoil.

When a ballot is found with the counterfoil attached, the deputy returning officer shall, while concealing the number on it from all persons present and without examining it, remove and destroy the counterfoil.

Section.Text: Sections 285 and 286 of the Act are replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Ballots not initialled by election officer
