Section.Text: If the election officer who counts the votes determines that a ballot has not been initialed by an election officer, he or she shall, in the presence of the election officer referred to in paragraph 283(1)(a) and witnesses, initial and count the ballot if satisfied that all ballots that were provided by the returning officer have been accounted for, as described in paragraph 283(3)(d).

Subsection.Text: One of the election officers referred to in subsection 283(1) shall make a record, in the prescribed form, of every objection to a ballot made by a candidate or candidate's representative, give a number to the objection, write that number on the ballot and initial it.

Every question that is raised by the objection shall be decided by the election officer who counts the votes, and the decision is subject to reversal only on a recount or on application under subsection 524(1).

Section.Text: If the deputy returning officer determines that he or she has failed to initial a ballot, the deputy returning officer shall, in the presence of the poll clerk and witnesses, initial and count the ballot if he or she is satisfied that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the ballot was supplied by him or her; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: all ballots that were provided by the returning officer have been accounted for, as described in paragraph 283(3)(d).

Subsection.Text: The deputy returning officer shall keep a record, in the prescribed form, of every objection to a ballot made by a candidate or his or her representatives, give a number to the objection, write that number on the ballot and initial it.

The deputy returning officer shall decide every question that is raised by an objection described in subsection (1), and the decision is subject to reversal only on a recount or on application under subsection 524(1).
Subsection 287(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

The election officer who counts the votes shall prepare a statement of the vote, in the prescribed form, that sets out the number of votes in favour of each candidate and the number of rejected ballots and shall place the original statement and a copy of it in the separate envelopes supplied for the purpose.

The deputy returning officer shall prepare a statement of the vote, in the prescribed form, that sets out the number of votes in favour of each candidate and the number of rejected ballots and place the original statement and a copy of it in the separate envelopes supplied for the purpose.
The deputy returning officer shall give a copy of the statement of the vote to each of the candidate's representatives present at the count.
Subsection 287(2) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:
The election officer shall give a copy of the statement of the vote to each of the candidates' representatives present at the count.
Subsections 288(1) and (2) of the Act are replaced by the following:

One of the election officers referred to in subsection 283(1) shall place the ballots for each candidate into separate envelopes, write on each envelope the name of the candidate and the number of votes he or she received, and seal it. The election officers shall sign the seal on each envelope, and the witnesses may also sign them.
One of the election officers shall place into separate envelopes the rejected ballots, the registration certificates and the list of electors, and shall seal the envelopes.

The deputy returning officer shall place the ballots for each candidate into separate envelopes, write on each envelope the name of the candidate and the number of votes he or she received, and seal it. The deputy returning officer and the poll clerk shall sign the seal on each envelope, and the witnesses may also sign them.
The deputy returning officer shall place into separate envelopes the rejected ballots, the registration certificates and the list of electors, and shall seal the envelopes.
The portion of subsection 288(3) of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:
One of the election officers shall seal in a large envelope supplied for the purpose
The deputy returning officer shall seal in a large envelope supplied for the purpose
Subsection 288(5) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:
The ballot box shall be sealed with the seals provided by the Chief Electoral Officer.
The ballot box shall be sealed by the deputy returning officer with the seals provided by the Chief Electoral Officer.

Section.Text: Sections 288.01 and 288.1 of the Act are replaced by the following:

One of the election officers referred to in subsection 283(1) shall place the form for each solemn declaration made under subsection 143(3) or paragraph 161(1)(b) or 169(2)(b) in an envelope supplied for the purpose.

Section.MarginalNote: Periodic statements of electors who voted
Section.Text: One of the election officers referred to in subsection 283(1) shall place a copy of each document prepared for the purpose of paragraph 162(i.1) in an envelope supplied for the purpose.
The deputy returning officer shall place the form for each oath taken under subsection 143(3) or paragraph 161(1)(b) or 169(2)(b) in an envelope supplied for the purpose.
The deputy returning officer shall place a copy of each document prepared for the purpose of paragraph 162(i.1) in an envelope supplied for the purpose.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 289(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Counting of votes on polling day

Subsection.Text: At least two election officers who are assigned to an advance polling station and who are specified in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's instructions shall, at the close of the polling stations on polling day, attend at the place mentioned in the notice of advance poll in subparagraph 172(a)(iii) to count the votes.

The deputy returning officer of an advance poll shall, at the close of the polling stations on polling day, attend with the poll clerk at the place mentioned in the notice of advance poll in subparagraph 172(a)(iii) to count the votes.
Paragraph 289(2)(a) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: for the application of paragraph 283(3)(e), the two or more election officers who are specified in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's instructions shall open the ballot boxes and empty their contents onto a table; and

Subsection.Text: Subsections 283(1) and (2), paragraphs 283(3)(e) and (f) and sections 284 to 288 apply with any necessary modifications to the counting of the votes of an advance poll except that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: for the application of paragraph 283(3)(e), the deputy returning officer shall open the ballot boxes and empty their contents onto a table; and

Subsection.Text: Subsection 289(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:
Subject to subsection (4), no person shall make a count of the votes cast at an advance poll before the close of voting hours on polling day.

The two or more election officers who are specified in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's instructions may begin counting the votes cast at an advance poll one hour before the close of voting hours on polling day if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the returning officer who is responsible for the advance polling station has obtained the Chief Electoral Officer's prior approval for the counting to begin;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the counting is done in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's instructions;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the counting is done in a manner that ensures the integrity of the vote; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the counting is done in the presence of any candidates or their representatives who are present or, if no candidates or representatives are present, at least two electors.

Subsection.Text: No person shall make a count of the votes cast at an advance poll before the close of the polling stations on polling day.

Section.Text: Sections 290 and 291 of the Act are replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Sending ballot boxes and envelopes to returning officer
Section.Text: An election officer who is assigned to a polling station or an advance polling station shall, without delay after sealing the ballot box, send to the returning officer the box, with the envelope that contains the original statement of the vote, the envelope that contains the registration certificates, the envelope referred to in section 288.01 and, in the case of an election officer who is assigned to a polling station, the envelope referred to in section 288.1.

A returning officer shall — on the request of the candidate, his or her representative or a representative of the candidate's party — provide him or her, after polling day, with one copy of each statement of the vote in respect of the candidate's electoral district.

Subsection.Text: The deputy returning officer for a polling station or an advance polling station shall, without delay after sealing the ballot box, send the box, with the envelope that contains the original statement of the vote, the envelope that contains the registration certificates, the envelope referred to in section 288.01 and, in the case of the deputy returning officer for a polling station, the envelope referred to in section 288.1 to the returning officer.

A returning officer may appoint persons to collect ballot boxes together with the envelopes referred to in subsection (1) from polling stations, and any person so appointed shall take the prescribed oath when he or she sends those materials to the returning officer.

Section.Text: A returning officer shall — on the request of the candidate, his or her representative or a representative of the candidate's party — provide him or her, after polling day, with

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: one copy of each statement of the vote in respect of the candidate's electoral district; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: one copy of the documents prepared under paragraph 162(i.1).

Section.Text: Section 292.1 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: List of persons who made solemn declaration
Section.Text: A returning officer, on the receipt of each envelope referred to in section 288.01, shall create a list of the names of all persons who made a solemn declaration under subsection 143(3) or paragraph 161(1)(b) or 169(2)(b) and shall include in the list the address of each of those persons.

A returning officer, on the receipt of each envelope referred to in section 288.01, shall create a list of the names of all persons who took an oath under subsection 143(3) or paragraph 161(1)(b) or 169(2)(b) and shall include in the list the address of each of those persons.
Paragraphs 296(2)(b) and (c) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: for ascertaining the total number of votes under paragraph (a), may summon any election officer or other person to appear before him or her at a fixed date and time and to bring with them all necessary documents; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: may question the election officer or other person respecting the matter in question and, if necessary, ask them to make a solemn declaration in respect of the matter.

Subsection.Text: If the returning officer is unable to obtain either the original statement of the vote or the ballot box, he or she

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: for ascertaining the total number of votes under paragraph (a), may summon any deputy returning officer, poll clerk or other person to appear before him or her at a fixed date and time and to bring with them all necessary documents; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: may examine on oath the deputy returning officer, poll clerk or other person respecting the matter in question.

Subsection.Text: Section 301 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (1):
The returning officer shall notify each candidate or his or her official agent in writing of the application for a recount.
The portion of subsection 301(2) of the French version of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:
Le juge fixe la date du dépouillement s'il appert, d'après l'affidavit d'un témoin digne de foi, que l'une ou l'autre des situations suivantes existe :
The judge shall fix a date for a recount if it appears, on the affidavit of a credible witness, that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a deputy returning officer has incorrectly counted or rejected any ballots, or has written an incorrect number on the statement of the vote for the votes cast for a candidate; or

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 301(2)(a) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: an election officer has incorrectly counted or rejected any ballots, or has written an incorrect number on the statement of the vote for the votes cast for a candidate; or

Subsection.Text: Subsection 304(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

The judge shall conduct the recount by adding the number of votes reported in the statements of the vote or by counting the valid ballots or all of the ballots returned by election officers or the Chief Electoral Officer.

The judge shall conduct the recount by adding the number of votes reported in the statements of the vote or by counting the valid ballots or all of the ballots returned by the deputy returning officers or the Chief Electoral Officer.
Subsection 304(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:
In the case of a recount conducted by counting the valid ballots or all of the ballots returned by election officers or the Chief Electoral Officer, the procedure set out in Schedule 4 applies.

In the case of a recount conducted by counting the valid ballots or all of the ballots returned by the deputy returning officers or the Chief Electoral Officer, the procedure set out in Schedule 4 applies.
Subsection 304(5) of the Act is replaced by the following:

For the purpose of conducting a recount, a judge has the power to summon any election officer as a witness and to require him or her to give evidence on oath and, for that purpose, has the same power that is vested in any court of record.

For the purpose of conducting a recount, a judge has the power to summon any deputy returning officer or poll clerk as a witness and to require him or her to give evidence on oath and, for that purpose, has the same power that is vested in any court of record.

Section.Text: Section 308 of the Act is amended by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (b) and by replacing paragraph (c) with the following:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: return to the returning officer the election documents or election materials brought under subsection 300(4) or 301(4) for the purpose of the recount; and
deliver to the returning officer the reports created in the course of the recount.

Section.Text: At the conclusion of a recount, the judge shall

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: return to the returning officer the election documents or other election materials brought for the purpose of the recount under subsection 300(4) and deliver to him or her the reports created in the course of the recount.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 311(2) of the French version of the Act is replaced by the following:
La requête peut être appuyée par un affidavit, qu'il n'est pas nécessaire d'intituler d'aucune manière, exposant les faits qui se rattachent au défaut de conformité.
An application under subsection (1) may be made on affidavit, which need not be entitled in any matter or cause, that sets out the facts relating to the failure to comply.
Subsection 311(4) of the French version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Le juge visé ou toute partie intéressée peuvent déposer au bureau du greffier, du registraire ou du protonotaire du tribunal du juge auquel la requête a été présentée des affidavits en réponse à ceux que le requérant a produits; sur demande, ils en fournissent des copies au requérant.

The judge complained of and any interested party may file in the office of the clerk, registrar or prothonotary of the court of the judge to whom the application is made affidavits in reply to those filed by the applicant and shall provide the applicant with copies of them on demand.
Paragraph 314(1)(a) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a report of the returning officer's proceedings in the prescribed form including his or her comments with respect to the state of the election documents received from election officers;

Subsection.Text: On completing the return of the writ, the returning officer shall without delay send to the Chief Electoral Officer all election documents in his or her possession together with

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a report of the returning officer's proceedings in the prescribed form including his or her comments with respect to the state of the election documents received from the deputy returning officers;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: all other documents that were used at the election.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 314(1)(c) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: all other documents that were used at the election, including documents prepared under paragraph 162(i.1).

Section.Text: The definitions election advertising and election survey in section 319 of the Act are repealed.

Definition.Text: election advertising means the transmission to the public by any means during an election period of an advertising message that promotes or opposes a registered party or the election of a candidate, including one that takes a position on an issue with which a registered party or candidate is associated. For greater certainty, it does not include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the transmission to the public of an editorial, a debate, a speech, an interview, a column, a letter, a commentary or news;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the distribution of a book, or the promotion of the sale of a book, for no less than its commercial value, if the book was planned to be made available to the public regardless of whether there was to be an election;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the transmission of a document directly by a person or a group to their members, employees or shareholders, as the case may be;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the transmission by an individual, on a non-commercial basis on what is commonly known as the Internet, of his or her personal political views; or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the making of telephone calls to electors only to encourage them to vote. (publicité électorale)

Definition.Text: election survey means an opinion survey of how electors voted or will vote at an election or respecting an issue with which a registered party or candidate is associated. (sondage électoral)

Section.Text: Section 321 of the Act is repealed.

Subsection.Text: No person shall knowingly conduct election advertising or cause it to be conducted using a means of transmission of the Government of Canada.
For the purpose of subsection (1), a person includes a group within the meaning of Part 17.

Section.Text: Subsection 323(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: No person shall transmit election advertising to the public in an electoral district on polling day before the close of all of the polling stations in the electoral district.
No person shall knowingly transmit election advertising to the public in an electoral district on polling day before the close of all of the polling stations in the electoral district.

Section.Text: The heading before section 326 of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: Subsection 326(1) of the Act is amended by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (e), by adding "and" at the end of paragraph (f) and by adding the following after paragraph (f):

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: the address of the Internet site on which a report referred to in subsection (3) is published.

Subsection.Text: The first person who transmits the results of an election survey — other than a survey that is described in section 327 — to the public during an election period and any person who transmits them to the public within 24 hours after they are first transmitted to the public must provide the following together with the results:
Subsection 326(2) of the Act is replaced by the following:

In addition to the information referred to in subsection (1), in the case of a transmission to the public by means other than broadcasting, the wording of the survey questions in respect of which data is obtained must be provided.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Notice of transmission of survey results
Subsection.Text: The first person who transmits to the public the results of an election survey — other than a survey that is described in section 327 — shall, if that person is not the sponsor of the survey, ensure that the sponsor of the survey has been notified, before the transmission, of the date on which the results are to be transmitted.
In addition to the information referred to in subsection (1), the following must be provided in the case of a transmission to the public by means other than broadcasting:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the wording of the survey questions in respect of which data is obtained; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the means by which a report referred to in subsection (3) may be obtained.

Subsection.Text: The portion of subsection 326(3) of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:

A sponsor of an election survey — other than a survey that is described in section 327 — shall, during an election period, ensure that a report on the results of the survey is published and remains for the remainder of that period on an Internet site that is available to the public. The sponsor shall do so before transmitting the results of the survey, if they are the first person to transmit them or, if they are not, as soon as feasible after being notified of the date of transmission under subsection (2.1), and the report shall include the following, as applicable:

A sponsor of an election survey shall, at any time during an election period after the results of the survey are transmitted to the public, provide, on request, a copy of a written report on the results of the survey, as transmitted under subsection (1). The report shall include the following, as applicable:
Subsection 326(4) of the Act is repealed.
A sponsor may charge a fee of up to $0.25 per page for a copy of a report provided under subsection (3).

Section.Text: Subsection 328(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — causing transmission of election survey results during blackout period

Subsection.Text: No person shall cause to be transmitted to the public, in an electoral district on polling day before the close of all of the polling stations in that electoral district, the results of an election survey that have not previously been transmitted to the public.

No person shall knowingly cause to be transmitted to the public, in an electoral district on polling day before the close of all of the polling stations in that electoral district, the results of an election survey that have not previously been transmitted to the public.

Section.Text: Subsection 330(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — use of broadcasting station outside Canada

Subsection.Text: No person shall, with intent to influence persons to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at an election, use a broadcasting station outside Canada, or aid, abet, counsel or procure the use of a broadcasting station outside Canada, during an election period, for the broadcasting of any matter having reference to an election.
Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of any matter that is broadcast if the broadcasting signals originated in Canada.

No person shall, with intent to influence persons to vote or refrain from voting or vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate at an election, use, aid, abet, counsel or procure the use of a broadcasting station outside Canada, during an election period, for the broadcasting of any matter having reference to an election.

Section.Text: Section 331 of the Act and the heading before it are repealed.

ExplanatoryNote.Label: Clause 213:
ExplanatoryNote.ExplanatoryText: Existing text of the heading and section 331:

Section.Text: No person who does not reside in Canada shall, during an election period, in any way induce electors to vote or refrain from voting or vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate unless the person is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a Canadian citizen; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a permanent resident within the meaning of subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 348.06(2)(b) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the name of the person or group that is a party to the agreement;

Subsection.Text: For each election period to which the agreement applies, the registration notice shall be filed not later than 48 hours after the first call is made under the agreement and shall set out

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the name of the person or group with which the calling service provider has entered into the agreement; and

Subsection.Text: Subsection 348.06(2) of the Act is amended by adding the following after paragraph (b):

Paragraph.Label: (b.1)
Paragraph.Text: the name of the person or group on whose behalf calls will be made under the agreement; and

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 348.07(2)(b) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the name of the person or group that is a party to the agreement;

Subsection.Text: For each election period to which the agreement applies, the registration notice shall be filed not later than 48 hours after the first call is made under the agreement and shall set out

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the name of the person or group with which the calling service provider has entered into the agreement; and

Subsection.Text: Subsection 348.07(2) of the Act is amended by adding the following after paragraph (b):

Paragraph.Label: (b.1)
Paragraph.Text: the name of the person or group on whose behalf calls will be made under the agreement; and

Section.Text: Section 348.12 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: As soon as feasible but no later than 30 days after polling day, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission shall, in the manner that it considers appropriate, publish the registration notices relating to the election that have been filed with it.

Nothing in subsection (1) precludes the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission from publishing, before polling day, any registration notice filed with it or any information related to any incomplete registration notice that is filed with it.

Section.Text: As soon as feasible after the expiry of 30 days after polling day, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission shall, in the manner that it considers appropriate, publish the registration notices relating to the election that have been filed with it.
The heading of Division 2 of Part 16.1 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Heading.TitleText: Scripts, Recordings and Lists of Telephone Numbers

Section.Text: Section 348.16 of the Act is amended by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (a), by adding "and" at the end of paragraph (b) and by adding the following after paragraph (b):

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a list of every telephone number called under the agreement during the election period.

Section.Text: Every calling service provider that, in accordance with an agreement, provides voter contact calling services shall keep, for three years after the end of the election period,
Section 348.17 of the Act is amended by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (a), by adding "and" at the end of paragraph (b) and by adding the following after paragraph (b):

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a list of every telephone number called under the agreement during the election period.

Section.Text: Every person or group that enters into an agreement with a calling service provider under which voter contact calling services are provided shall keep, for one year after the end of the election period,
Sections 348.18 and 348.19 of the Act are replaced by the following:

If, during an election period, a person or group uses their internal services to make calls by means of an automatic dialing-announcing device for any purpose relating to the election, including a purpose referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the definition voter contact calling services in section 348.01, the person or group shall keep, for one year after the end of the election period,

Paragraph.Text: a recording of each unique message conveyed by the device and a record of every date on which it was so conveyed; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a list of every telephone number called for that purpose during the election period.

Section.MarginalNote: Third party that is corporation or group — internal services
Section.Text: If, during an election period, a third party that is a corporation or group uses its internal services to make live voice calls for any purpose relating to the election, including a purpose referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the definition voter contact calling services in section 348.01, the third party shall, if a script is used, keep, for one year after the end of the election period,

Paragraph.Text: a copy of each unique script used and a record of every date on which the script was used; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a list of every telephone number called for that purpose during the election period.

Section.Text: If, during an election period, a person or group uses their internal services to make calls by means of an automatic dialing-announcing device for any purpose relating to the election, including a purpose referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the definition voter contact calling services in section 348.01, the person or group shall keep a recording of each unique message conveyed by the device and a record of every date on which it was so conveyed, for one year after the end of the election period.

If, during an election period, a third party that is a corporation or group uses its internal services to make live voice calls for any purpose relating to the election, including a purpose referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the definition voter contact calling services in section 348.01, the third party shall, if a script is used, keep a copy of each unique script used and a record of every date on which the script was used, for one year after the end of the election period.
The heading of Part 17 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Heading.TitleText: Third Party Advertising, Partisan Activities and Election Surveys

Subsection.Text: The definitions election advertising and election advertising expense in section 349 of the Act are repealed.

Definition.Text: election advertising has the same meaning as in section 319. (publicité électorale)
election advertising expense means an expense incurred in relation to

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the production of an election advertising message; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the acquisition of the means of transmission to the public of an election advertising message. (dépenses de publicité électorale)

Subsection.Text: The definition third party in section 349 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Definition.Text: third party means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in Division 1, a person or a group other than

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a registered party or eligible party or a registered association,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a potential candidate within the meaning of paragraph (a), (b) or (d) of the definition potential candidate in subsection 2(1), or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: a nomination contestant; and

Paragraph.Text: in Division 2, a person or a group other than a candidate, a registered party or an electoral district association of a registered party. (tiers)

Definition.Text: third party means a person or a group, other than a candidate, registered party or electoral district association of a registered party. (tiers)

Subsection.Text: Section 349 of the Act is amended by adding the following in alphabetical order:

Definition.Text: election survey means an election survey that is conducted by, or caused to be conducted by, a third party — a person or group other than a political party that is registered under an Act of a province — during a pre-election period or an election period and whose results the person or group takes into account

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in deciding whether or not to organize and carry out partisan activities or to transmit partisan advertising messages or election advertising messages; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in their organization and carrying out of those activities or their transmission of those messages. (sondage électoral)

Definition.Text: election survey expense means an expense incurred in respect of the conducting of an election survey

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in Division 1, during a pre-election period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in Division 2, during an election period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in Division 3, during either a pre-election period or an election period. (dépenses de sondage électoral)

Definition.Text: partisan activity means an activity, including canvassing door-to-door, making telephone calls to electors and organizing rallies, that is carried out by a third party — a person or group other than a political party that is registered under an Act of a province — and that promotes or opposes a registered party or eligible party or the election of a potential candidate, nomination contestant, candidate or leader of a registered party or eligible party, otherwise than by taking a position on an issue with which any such party or person is associated. It does not include election advertising, partisan advertising or a fundraising activity. (activité partisane)
partisan activity expense means an expense incurred in respect of the organization and carrying out of a partisan activity. (dépenses d'activité partisane)
registered third party means a third party that is registered under section 349.6 or 353. (tiers enregistré)

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 349:

Heading.Label: DIVISION 1
Heading.TitleText: Partisan Activities, Partisan Advertising and Election Surveys During Pre-election Period

Subsection.Text: Subject to section 349.4, a third party shall not incur the following expenses in an aggregate amount of more than $700,000:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan activities that are carried out during a pre-election period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: partisan advertising expenses in relation to partisan advertising messages that are transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: election survey expenses in relation to election surveys that are conducted during that period.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Maximum pre-election period expenses — electoral district
Subsection.Text: Not more than $7,000 of the maximum amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be incurred to promote or oppose the election of one or more potential candidates or nomination contestants in a given electoral district.

The maximum amount set out in subsection (2) only applies to an amount incurred with respect to a leader of a registered party or eligible party to the extent that it is incurred to promote or oppose his or her election in an electoral district.
The amounts referred to in subsections (1) and (2) shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor referred to in section 384 that is in effect on the first day of the pre-election period.

Section.Text: A third party shall not circumvent, or attempt to circumvent, a maximum amount set out in section 349.1 in any manner, including by splitting itself into two or more third parties for the purpose of circumventing the maximum amount or acting in collusion with another third party so that their combined partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses exceed the maximum amount.

Subsection.Text: No third party and no registered party shall act in collusion with each other — including by sharing information — in order to influence the third party in its partisan activities that it carries out during a pre-election period, its partisan advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be conducted during a pre-election period.

No third party and no potential candidate shall act in collusion with each other — including by sharing information — in order to influence the third party in its partisan activities that it carries out during a pre-election period, its partisan advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be conducted during a pre-election period.

No third party and no person associated with a potential candidate's activities undertaken with a view to the potential candidate's eventual election — including an official agent of a potential candidate who is deemed to be a candidate under section 477 — shall act in collusion with each other — including by sharing information — in order to influence the third party in its partisan activities that it carries out during a pre-election period, its partisan advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be conducted during a pre-election period.

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — spending by foreign third parties

Subsection.Text: A foreign third party shall not incur the following expenses:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in relation to a partisan activity that is carried out during a pre-election period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: partisan advertising expenses in relation to a partisan advertising message that is transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: election survey expenses in relation to an election survey that is conducted during that period.

Subsection.Text: In subsection (1), a foreign third party is a third party in respect of which

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is an individual, the individual

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is not a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: is not a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: does not reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a corporation or entity,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: it does not carry on business in Canada, or its only activity carried on in Canada during a pre-election period consists of doing anything to influence electors during that period to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the following election, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: it was incorporated, formed or otherwise organized outside Canada; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a group, no person who is responsible for the group

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: is a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: resides in Canada.

Section.Text: A third party shall identify itself in any partisan advertising message placed by it and mention in or on the message that it has authorized its transmission.

Subsection.Text: A third party shall register immediately after having incurred the following expenses in an aggregate amount of $500:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan activities that are carried out during a pre-election period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: partisan advertising expenses in relation to partisan advertising messages that are transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: election survey expenses in relation to election surveys that are conducted during that period.

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: However, the third party may not register before the beginning of the pre-election period.

Subsection.Text: An application for registration shall be sent to the Chief Electoral Officer in the prescribed form and shall include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is an individual, the individual's name, address and telephone number, their signature and their declaration that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: they reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a corporation, the name, address and telephone number of the corporation and of an officer who has signing authority for it, the officer's signature and their declaration that the corporation carries on business in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a group, the name, address and telephone number of the group and of a person who is responsible for the group, the person's signature and their declaration that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: they reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the address and telephone number of the third party's office where its books and records are kept and of the office in Canada to which communications may be addressed and at which documents may be served; and

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the name, address and telephone number of the third party's financial agent.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Declaration of financial agent to accompany application
Subsection.Text: An application under subsection (2) shall be accompanied by a declaration signed by the financial agent accepting the appointment.

If a third party's financial agent is replaced, it shall, without delay, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the new financial agent's name, address and telephone number and a declaration signed by the new financial agent accepting the appointment.

If the third party is a trade union, corporation or other entity with a governing body, the application shall include a copy of a resolution passed by its governing body authorizing it to incur partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses.

The Chief Electoral Officer shall, without delay after receiving an application, determine whether the requirements set out in subsections (1) to (3) and (5) are met and shall then notify the person who signed the application whether the third party is registered. In the case of a refusal to register, the Chief Electoral Officer shall give reasons for the refusal.

A third party may not be registered under a name that, in the Chief Electoral Officer's opinion, is likely to be confused with the name of a registered party or eligible party, a potential candidate, a nomination contestant, a candidate, a leadership contestant, a leader of a registered party or eligible party or a registered third party.

Subject to subsection 353(1.1), the registration of a third party is valid only for the pre-election period during which the application is made, but the third party continues to be subject to this Part.

A third party that is required to register under subsection 349.6(1) shall appoint a financial agent, who may be a person who is authorized to sign an application for registration made under that subsection.
The following persons are not eligible to be a financial agent of a third party:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: an election officer or a member of the staff of a returning officer;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a potential candidate or — if the potential candidate is deemed to be a candidate under section 477 — their official agent;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the chief agent of a registered party or eligible party;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a registered agent of a registered party;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: a nomination contestant or their financial agent;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: a leadership contestant or their leadership campaign agent; and

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: a person who is not a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

Subsection.Text: A third party that is required to register under subsection 349.6(1) shall appoint an auditor without delay if it incurs the following expenses in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan activities that are carried out during a pre-election period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: partisan advertising expenses in relation to partisan advertising messages that are transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: election survey expenses in relation to election surveys that are conducted during that period.

Subsection.Text: The following are eligible to be an auditor for a third party:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a person who is a member in good standing of a corporation, an association or an institute of professional accountants; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a partnership every partner of which is a member in good standing of a corporation, an association or an institute of professional accountants.

Subsection.Text: The following persons are not eligible to be an auditor for a third party:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the third party's financial agent;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a person who signed the application made under subsection 349.6(2);

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an election officer or a member of the staff of a returning officer;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a potential candidate or — if the potential candidate is deemed to be a candidate under section 477 — their official agent;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the chief agent of a registered party or eligible party;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: a registered agent of a registered party;

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: a nomination contestant or their financial agent; and

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: a leadership contestant or their leadership campaign agent.

Subsection.Text: Every third party, without delay after an auditor is appointed, shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the auditor's name, address, telephone number and occupation and a declaration signed by the auditor accepting the appointment.

If a third party's auditor is replaced, it shall, without delay, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the new auditor's name, address, telephone number and occupation and a declaration signed by the new auditor accepting the appointment.

Every contribution made during a pre-election period to a registered third party for partisan activity, partisan advertising or election survey purposes shall be accepted by its financial agent, and every partisan activity expense, partisan advertising expense or election survey expense incurred during a pre-election period on behalf of a registered third party shall be authorized by its financial agent.

A financial agent may authorize a person to accept contributions or to authorize the incurring of partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses or election survey expenses, but that authorization does not limit the financial agent's responsibility.

Every third party that is required to be registered in accordance with subsection 349.6(1) shall file an interim third-party expenses return in the prescribed form with the Chief Electoral Officer within 5 days after the day on which it became required to be registered in accordance with that subsection, if the third party

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: has incurred expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(1) in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more during the period beginning on the day after polling day at the general election previous to the pre-election period and ending on the day on which it became required to be registered in accordance with subsection 349.6(1); or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: has received contributions in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election survey purposes during the period referred to in paragraph (a).

Subsection.Text: The interim third-party expenses return shall contain

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a list of partisan activity expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(2) incurred during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a) and the date and place of the partisan activities to which the expenses relate;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a list of partisan advertising expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(2) incurred during that period and the date and place of the transmission of the partisan advertising messages to which the expenses relate;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a list of election survey expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(2) incurred during that period and the date of the election surveys to which the expenses relate; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a list of all partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(1) incurred during that period — other than those referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c) — and the date and place of the partisan activities to which the partisan activity expenses relate, the date and place of the transmission of the partisan advertising messages to which the partisan advertising expenses relate and the date of the election surveys to which the election survey expenses relate.

Subsection.Text: If a third party has not incurred expenses referred to in subsection (2), that fact shall be indicated in its interim third-party expenses return.
The interim third-party expenses return shall include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, by class of contributor, of contributions for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election survey purposes that were received during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: subject to paragraph (c), for each contributor who made contributions of a total amount of more than $200 for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election survey purposes during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a), their name, address and class, and the amount and date of each contribution;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a numbered company that is a contributor referred to in paragraph (b), the name of the chief executive officer or president of that company; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, other than an amount of a contribution referred to in paragraph (a), that was paid out of the third party's own funds during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a) for partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

Subsection.Text: The interim third-party expenses return need not include any information referred to in subsections (2) and (4) that was included in a third-party expenses return that the third party previously filed under subsection 359(1) in respect of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a by-election that was held after the general election referred to in paragraph (1)(a); or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a general election for which the third party incurred expenses or received contributions between the day fixed under paragraph 57(1.2)(c) for polling day at the general election and polling day in an electoral district in which the election was postponed under subsection 59(4) or 77(1).

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of subsection (4), a contribution includes a loan.
For the purposes of paragraphs (4)(a) and (b), the following are the classes of contributor:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: individuals;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: businesses;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: commercial organizations;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: governments;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: trade unions;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: corporations without share capital other than trade unions; and

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: unincorporated organizations or associations other than trade unions.

Subsection.Text: If the third party is unable to identify which contributions were received during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a) for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election survey purposes, the interim third-party expenses return shall include, subject to paragraph (4)(c), the names and addresses of every contributor who contributed a total of more than $200 to it during that period.
The interim third-party expenses return shall include a declaration that the return is accurate signed by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the third party's financial agent; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if different from the financial agent, the person who signed the application made under subsection 349.6(2).

Subsection.Text: A third party shall, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officer, provide documents evidencing expenses set out in the return that are in an amount of more than $50, including bank statements, deposit slips and cancelled cheques.

Every third party that is required to be registered in accordance with subsection 349.6(1) shall file an interim third-party expenses return in the prescribed form with the Chief Electoral Officer on September 15, if the third party

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: has incurred expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(1) in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more during the period beginning on the day after polling day at the general election previous to the pre-election period and ending on the earlier of September 14 and the last day of the pre-election period; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: has received contributions in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election survey purposes during the period referred to in paragraph (a).

Subsection.Text: Subsections 349.91(2) to (10) apply to the return under subsection (1), except that a reference to the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a) of section 349.91 shall be read as a reference to the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a) of this section.

In addition to the exceptions set out in subsection 349.91(5), the interim third-party expenses return need not include any information referred to in subsections 349.91(2) and (4) that was included in an interim third-party expenses return that the third party previously filed under subsection 349.91(1).
This section applies only in the case of a general election that is held on a day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2.

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — false, misleading or incomplete return
Section.Text: No third party shall file under subsection 349.91(1) or 349.92(1) an interim third-party expenses return that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the third party knows or ought reasonably to know contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: does not substantially set out the information required under section 349.91 or 349.92, as the case may be.

Section.Text: No third party shall use a contribution made for partisan activity, partisan advertising or election survey purposes for the purpose of any of the following if the third party does not know the name and address of the contributor or is otherwise unable to determine within which class of contributor referred to in subsection 349.91(7) the contributor falls:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a partisan activity that is carried out during a pre-election period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a partisan advertising message that is transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an election survey that is conducted during that period and whose results the third party takes into account in its decisions concerning whether or not to organize and carry out partisan activities during that period or to transmit partisan advertising messages during that period.

Section.Text: No third party shall use funds for any purpose set out in paragraphs 349.94(a) to (c) if the source of the funds is a foreign entity, including

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: an individual who is not a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a corporation or entity incorporated, formed or otherwise organized outside Canada that does not carry on business in Canada or whose only activity carried on in Canada during a pre-election period consists of doing anything to influence electors during that period to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the following election;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a trade union that does not hold bargaining rights for employees in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a foreign political party; or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: a foreign government or an agent or mandatary of one.

Heading.Label: DIVISION 2
Heading.TitleText: Partisan Activities, Election Advertising and Election Surveys During Election Period

Subsection.Text: Subsections 350(1) to (4.1) of the Act are replaced by the following:
Subject to section 351.1, a third party shall not incur the following expenses in an aggregate amount of more than $350,000:

Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan activities that are carried out during the election period of a general election;
election advertising expenses in relation to election advertising messages that are transmitted during that period; and
election survey expenses in relation to election surveys that are conducted during that period.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Maximum election period expenses — electoral district
Subsection.Text: Not more than $3,000 of the maximum amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be incurred to promote or oppose the election of one or more candidates in a given electoral district.

The maximum amount set out in subsection (2) only applies to an amount incurred with respect to a leader of a registered party or eligible party to the extent that it is incurred to promote or oppose his or her election in an electoral district.
Subject to section 351.1, a third party shall not incur the following expenses in an aggregate amount of more than $3,000 in a given electoral district:

Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan activities that are carried out during the election period of a by-election;
election advertising expenses in relation to election advertising messages that are transmitted during that period; and
election survey expenses in relation to election surveys that are conducted during that period.

Subsection.Text: In the case of a general election that is not held on a day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2, or of a by-election, a third party is deemed not to have incurred a partisan activity expense, an election advertising expense or an election survey expense if, on the issue of the writ or writs, it is not able to cancel the activity, the transmission of the advertising message or the survey, as the case may be, that the expense is in relation to.
Subject to section 351.1, a third party shall not incur election advertising expenses of a total amount of more than $150,000 in relation to a general election.
Not more than $3,000 of the total amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be incurred to promote or oppose the election of one or more candidates in a given electoral district, including by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: naming them;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: showing their likenesses;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: identifying them by their respective political affiliations; or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: taking a position on an issue with which they are particularly associated.

Subsection.Text: The limit set out in subsection (2) only applies to an amount incurred with respect to a leader of a registered party or eligible party to the extent that it is incurred to promote or oppose his or her election in a given electoral district.
Subject to section 351.1, a third party shall not incur election advertising expenses of a total amount of more than $3,000 in a given electoral district in relation to a by-election.

If a general election is held on a date other than one set out in subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2, or if a by-election is held, a third party does not incur an election advertising expense if, on the issue of the writ or writs, it is not able to cancel the transmission of that advertising.
The amounts referred to in subsections (1), (2) and (4) shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor referred to in section 384 that is in effect on the issue of the writ or writs.
If an election period is longer than 37 days, then the amounts referred to in subsections (1), (2) and (4) are increased by adding to them the product of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: one thirty-seventh of the amount referred to in subsection (1), (2) or (4), as the case may be, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the number of days in the election period minus 37.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 350(5) of the French version of the Act is replaced by the following:
Les sommes visées aux paragraphes (1), (2) et (4) sont multipliées par le facteur d'ajustement à l'inflation visé à l'article 384, applicable à la date de délivrance du ou des brefs.
Subsection 350(6) of the Act is repealed.

Section.Text: Sections 351 to 352 of the Act are replaced by the following:

A third party shall not circumvent, or attempt to circumvent, a maximum amount set out in section 350 in any manner, including by splitting itself into two or more third parties for the purpose of circumventing the maximum amount or acting in collusion with another third party so that their combined partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey expenses exceed the maximum amount.

Subsection.Text: No third party and no registered party shall act in collusion with each other — including by sharing information — in order to influence the third party in its partisan activities that it carries out during an election period, its election advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be conducted during an election period.

No third party and no candidate shall act in collusion with each other — including by sharing information — in order to influence the third party in its partisan activities that it carries out during an election period, its election advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be conducted during an election period.

No third party and no person associated with a candidate's campaign — including a candidate's official agent — shall act in collusion with each other — including by sharing information — in order to influence the third party in its partisan activities that it carries out during an election period, its election advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be conducted during an election period.

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — spending by foreign third parties

Subsection.Text: A foreign third party shall not incur the following expenses:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in relation to a partisan activity that is carried out during an election period;
election advertising expenses in relation to an election advertising message that is transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: election survey expenses in relation to an election survey that is conducted during that period.

Text.Ins: In subsection (1), a foreign third party is a third party in respect of which

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is an individual, the individual

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is not a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: is not a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: does not reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a corporation or entity,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: it does not carry on business in Canada, or its only activity carried on in Canada during an election period consists of doing anything to influence electors during that period to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the election, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: it was incorporated, formed or otherwise organized outside Canada; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a group, no person who is responsible for the group

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: is a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: resides in Canada.

Section.Text: A third party shall identify itself in any election advertising message placed by it and shall mention in or on the message that it has authorized its transmission.

A third party shall not circumvent, or attempt to circumvent, a limit set out in section 350 in any manner, including by splitting itself into two or more third parties for the purpose of circumventing the limit or acting in collusion with another third party so that their combined election advertising expenses exceed the limit.

A third party shall not incur election advertising expenses of a total amount of $500 or more in relation to a general election or a by-election, or, if the election periods of two or more by-elections overlap with each other in whole or in part, in relation to those by-elections, unless

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is an individual, the individual

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: is a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: resides in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a corporation, it carries on business in Canada; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a group, a person who is responsible for the group

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: is a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: resides in Canada.

Section.Text: For greater certainty, for the purposes of subsections 350(1) and (4) and section 351.1 if election advertising is transmitted during an election period, it shall be considered an election advertising expense, regardless of when it was incurred.
A third party shall identify itself in any election advertising placed by it and indicate that it has authorized the advertising.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 353(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:
A third party shall register immediately after having incurred the following expenses in an aggregate amount of $500:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan activities that are carried out during an election period;
election advertising expenses in relation to election advertising messages that are transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: election survey expenses in relation to election surveys that are conducted during that period.

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: However, the third party may not register before the issue of the writ.

Subsection.Text: A third party that registered under subsection 349.6(1) during a pre-election period that ends the day before the day of the issue of the writ and that is also required to register under subsection (1) is deemed to be registered under that subsection (1).
Subject to section 351.1, a third party shall register immediately after having incurred election advertising expenses of a total amount of $500 and may not register before the issue of the writ.
Paragraphs 353(2)(a) to (c) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is an individual, the individual's name, address and telephone number, their signature and their declaration that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: they reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a corporation, the name, address and telephone number of the corporation and of an officer who has signing authority for it, the officer's signature and their declaration that the corporation carries on business in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b.1)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a group, the name, address and telephone number of the group and of a person who is responsible for the group, the person's signature and their declaration that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: they reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the address and telephone number of the third party's office where its books and records are kept and of the office in Canada to which communications may be addressed and at which documents may be served; and

Subsection.Text: An application for registration shall be sent to the Chief Electoral Officer in the prescribed form and shall include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is an individual, the individual's name, address and telephone number, their signature and their certification that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: they reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a corporation, the name, address and telephone number of the corporation and of an officer who has signing authority for it, the officer's signature and their certification that the corporation carries on business in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (b.1)
Paragraph.Text: if the third party is a group, the name, address and telephone number of the group and of a person who is responsible for the group, the person's signature and their certification that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a Canadian citizen,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: they are a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: they reside in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the address and telephone number of the office of the third party where its books and records are kept and of the office to which communications may be addressed; and

Subsection.Text: Subsection 353(5) of the Act is replaced by the following:

If the third party is a trade union, corporation or other entity with a governing body, the application shall include a copy of a resolution passed by its governing body authorizing it to incur partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey expenses.

If the third party is a trade union, corporation or other entity with a governing body, the application must include a copy of the resolution passed by its governing body authorizing it to incur election advertising expenses.
Subsection 353(8) of the Act is replaced by the following:

The registration of a third party is valid only for the election period during which the application is made, but the third party continues to be subject to the requirement to file a third-party expenses return under subsection 359(1).

The registration of a third party is valid only for the election period during which the application is made, but the third party continues to be subject to the requirement to file an election advertising report under subsection 359(1).
Subsection 354(1) of the French version of the Act is replaced by the following:
Le tiers tenu de s'enregistrer en application du paragraphe 353(1) doit nommer un agent financier; celui-ci peut être la personne autorisée à signer la demande d'enregistrement visée à ce paragraphe.

A third party that is required to register under subsection 353(1) shall appoint a financial agent who may be a person who is authorized to sign an application for registration made under that subsection.
Section 354 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (1):

If, at the end of the pre-election period before a general election referred to in paragraph 353(1)(a), a third party has a financial agent who was appointed under subsection 349.7(1), the financial agent is deemed to have been appointed under subsection (1).
Paragraph 354(2)(c) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an election officer or a member of the staff of a returning officer; and

Subsection.Text: The following persons are not eligible to be a financial agent of a third party:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an election officer or an employee of a returning officer; and

Subsection.Text: Subsection 355(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:
A third party that is required to register under subsection 353(1) shall appoint an auditor without delay if it incurs the following expenses in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: partisan activity expenses in respect of partisan activities that take place during an election period;
election advertising expenses in respect of election advertising messages that are transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: election survey expenses in relation to that period.

Subsection.Text: If, when the obligation under subsection (1) to appoint an auditor applies, a third party has an auditor who was appointed under subsection 349.8(1), the auditor is deemed to have been appointed under subsection (1).
A third party that incurs election advertising expenses in an aggregate amount of $5,000 or more must appoint an auditor without delay.
Paragraph 355(3)(c) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an election officer or a member of the staff of a returning officer;

Subsection.Text: The following persons are not eligible to be an auditor for a third party:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an election officer;

Section.Text: Section 356 of the Act is repealed.

The Chief Electoral Officer shall maintain, for the period that he or she considers appropriate, a registry of third parties in which is recorded, in relation to each third party, the information referred to in subsections 353(2) and 355(4) and (5).

Subsection.Text: Subsection 357(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Every contribution made during an election period to a registered third party for partisan activity, election advertising or election survey purposes shall be accepted by its financial agent, and every partisan activity expense, election advertising expense and election survey expense incurred during an election period on behalf of a registered third party shall be authorized by its financial agent.

Every contribution made during an election period to a registered third party for election advertising purposes must be accepted by, and every election advertising expense incurred on behalf of a third party must be authorized by, its financial agent.
A financial agent may authorize a person to accept contributions or incur election advertising expenses, but that authorization does not limit the responsibility of the financial agent.

No third party shall use a contribution for election advertising if the third party does not know the name and address of the contributor or is otherwise unable to determine within which class of contributor referred to in subsection 359(6) they fall.
Subsection 357(2) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

A financial agent may authorize a person to accept contributions or to authorize the incurring of partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses, but that authorization does not limit the financial agent's responsibility.
Subsection 357(3) of the Act is repealed.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 357:

No third party shall use a contribution for the purpose of any of the following if the third party does not know the name and address of the contributor or is otherwise unable to determine within which class of contributor referred to in subsection 359(6) the contributor falls:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a partisan activity that is carried out during an election period;
an election advertising message that is transmitted during that period; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
