Paragraph.Text: an election survey that is conducted during that period and whose results the third party takes into account in its decisions concerning whether or not to organize and carry out partisan activities during that period or to transmit election advertising messages during that period.

Subsection.Text: The portion of section 358 of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:

Section.Text: No third party shall use funds for any purpose set out in paragraphs 357.1(a) to (c) if the source of the funds is a foreign entity, including
No third party shall use a contribution for election advertising purposes if the contribution is from

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a corporation or an association that does not carry on business in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: a foreign government or an agent of one.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 358(b) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a corporation or entity incorporated, formed or otherwise organized outside Canada that does not carry on business in Canada or whose only activity carried on in Canada during an election period consists of doing anything to influence electors during that period to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the election;

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 358(e) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: a foreign government or an agent or mandatary of one.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 358:

Heading.Label: DIVISION 3
Heading.TitleText: Third Parties' Bank Accounts, Registry of Third Parties and Third-Party Expenses Returns

Subsection.Text: A third party that is required to register under subsection 349.6(1) — or under subsection 353(1), if it was not required to register under subsection 349.6(1) — shall open a separate bank account for the sole purpose of its partisan activities that are carried out or to be carried out during a pre-election period or an election period, partisan advertising, election advertising and election surveys.

The account shall be in a Canadian financial institution as defined in section 2 of the Bank Act, or in an authorized foreign bank as defined in that section that is not subject to the restrictions and requirements referred to in subsection 524(2) of that Act.

All of the third party's financial transactions in relation to its partisan activities referred to in subsection (1), partisan advertising, election advertising and election surveys that involve the payment or receipt of money are to be paid from or deposited to the account.
After polling day, the third party shall close the account once all unpaid claims and any outstanding balance have been dealt with.
The third party shall, on closing the account, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the final statement of the account.

Section.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer shall maintain, for the period that he or she considers appropriate, a registry of registered third parties in which is recorded, in relation to each one, the information referred to in subsections 349.6(2), 349.8(4) and (5), 353(2) and 355(4) and (5).

Subsection.Text: Subsections 359(1) to (3) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Every third party that is required to be registered in accordance with subsection 349.6(1) or 353(1) shall file a third-party expenses return in the prescribed form with the Chief Electoral Officer within four months after polling day.
The third-party expenses return shall contain

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a general election that is held on a day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a list of partisan activity expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(2) and the date and place of the partisan activities to which the expenses relate,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a list of partisan advertising expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(2) and the date and place of the transmission of the partisan advertising messages to which the expenses relate,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: a list of election survey expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(2) and the date of the election surveys to which the expenses relate, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: a list of all partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses referred to in subsection 349.1(1) — other than those referred to in subparagraphs (i) to (iii) — and the date and place of the partisan activities to which the partisan activity expenses relate, the date and place of the transmission of the partisan advertising messages to which the partisan advertising expenses relate and the date of the election surveys to which the election survey expenses relate;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of any general election,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a list of partisan activity expenses referred to in subsection 350(2) and the date and place of the partisan activities to which the expenses relate,
a list of election advertising expenses referred to in subsection 350(2) and the date and place of the transmission of the election advertising messages to which the expenses relate,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: a list of election survey expenses referred to in subsection 350(2) and the date of the election surveys to which the expenses relate, and

a list of all partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey expenses referred to in subsection 350(1) other than those referred to in subparagraphs (i) to (iii) and the date and place of the partisan activities to which the partisan activity expenses relate, the date and place of the transmission of the election advertising messages to which the election advertising expenses relate and the date of the election surveys to which the election survey expenses relate; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a by-election, a list of partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey expenses referred to in subsection 350(4) and the date and place of the partisan activities to which the partisan activity expenses relate, the date and place of the transmission of the election advertising messages to which the election advertising expenses relate and the date of the election surveys to which the election survey expenses relate.

Subsection.Text: If a third party has not incurred expenses referred to in paragraph (2)(a), (b) or (c), that fact shall be indicated in its third-party expenses return.

Every third party that is required to be registered in accordance with subsection 353(1) shall file an election advertising report in the prescribed form with the Chief Electoral Officer within four months after polling day.
An election advertising report shall contain

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a general election,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a list of election advertising expenses referred to in subsection 350(2) and the time and place of the broadcast or publication of the advertisements to which the expenses relate, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a list of all election advertising expenses other than those referred to in subparagraph (i) and the time and place of broadcast or publication of the advertisements to which the expenses relate; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a by-election, a list of election advertising expenses referred to in subsection 350(4) and the time and place of the broadcast or publication of the advertisements to which the expenses relate.

Subsection.Text: If a third party has not incurred expenses referred to in paragraph (2)(a) or (b), that fact shall be indicated in its election advertising report.
The portion of subsection 359(4) of the Act before paragraph (b.1) is replaced by the following:
The third-party expenses return shall include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, by class of contributor, of contributions for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election survey purposes that were received during the period beginning the day after polling day at the general election previous to the polling day referred to in subsection (1) and ending on that polling day referred to in that subsection;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: subject to paragraph (b.1), for each contributor who made contributions of a total amount of more than $200 for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election survey purposes during the period referred to in paragraph (a), their name, address and class, and the amount and date of each contribution;

Subsection.Text: The election advertising report shall include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, by class of contributor, of contributions for election advertising purposes that were received in the period beginning six months before the issue of the writ and ending on polling day;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: for each contributor who made contributions of a total amount of more than $200 for election advertising purposes during the period referred to in paragraph (a), subject to paragraph (b.1), their name, address and class, and the amount and date of each contribution;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, other than an amount of a contribution referred to in paragraph (a), that was paid out of the third party's own funds for election advertising expenses.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 359(4)(c) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, other than an amount of a contribution referred to in paragraph (a), that was paid out of the third party's own funds for partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

Subsection.Text: Section 359 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (4):

The third-party expenses return need not include any information referred to in subsection (4) that was included in a third-party expenses return that the third party previously filed under subsection (1) in respect of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a by-election that was held after the general election referred to in paragraph (4)(a); or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a general election for which the third party incurred expenses or received contributions between the day fixed under paragraph 57(1.2)(c) for polling day at the general election and polling day in an electoral district in which the election was postponed under subsection 59(4) or 77(1).

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 359(6)(g) of the French version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: g)
Paragraph.Text: organismes ou associations non constitués en personne morale autres que les syndicats.

Provision.Text: For the purposes of paragraphs (4)(a) and (b), the following are the classes of contributor:

Provision.Label: (g)
Provision.Text: unincorporated organizations or associations other than trade unions.

Subsection.Text: Subsections 359(7) to (9) of the Act are replaced by the following:

If the third party is unable to identify which contributions were received during the period referred to in paragraph (4)(a) for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election survey purposes, the third-party expenses return shall include, subject to paragraph (4)(b.1), the names and addresses of every contributor who contributed a total of more than $200 to it during that period.
A third-party expenses return shall include a declaration that the return is accurate signed by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the third party's financial agent; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if different from the financial agent, the person who signed the application made under subsection 353(2) or — if subsection 353(1.1) applies — 349.6(2).

Subsection.Text: A third party shall, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officer, provide documents evidencing expenses set out in the return that are in an amount of more than $50, including bank statements, deposit slips and cancelled cheques.

If the third party is unable to identify which contributions were received for election advertising purposes in the period referred to in paragraph (4)(a), it must list, subject to paragraph (4)(b.1), the names and addresses of every contributor who donated a total of more than $200 to it during that period.

An election advertising report shall include the signed declarations of the financial agent and, if different, of the person who signed the application made under subsection 353(2) that the report is accurate.

A third party shall, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officer, provide the original of any bill, voucher or receipt in relation to an election advertising expense that is in an amount of more than $50.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 359:

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — false, misleading or incomplete document
Section.Text: No third party shall file under subsection 359(1) a third-party expenses return that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the third party knows or ought reasonably to know contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: does not substantially set out the information required under section 359.

Subsection.Text: Subsections 360(1) and (2) of the Act are replaced by the following:

If a third party incurs partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more, its third-party expenses return filed under subsection 359(1) shall include a report made under subsection (2).

The third party's auditor shall report on the third-party expenses return and shall make any examination that will enable the auditor to give an opinion in the report as to whether the return presents fairly the information contained in the accounting records on which it is based.
The election advertising report of a third party that incurs $5,000 or more in election advertising expenses must include a report made under subsection (2).

The third party's auditor shall report on the election advertising report and shall make any examination that will enable the auditor to give an opinion in the report as to whether the election advertising report presents fairly the information contained in the accounting records on which it is based.
Paragraph 360(3)(a) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the third-party expenses return that is the subject of the report does not present fairly the information contained in the accounting records on which it is based;

Subsection.Text: An auditor shall include in the report any statement that the auditor considers necessary, when

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the election advertising report that is the subject of the auditor's report does not present fairly the information contained in the accounting records on which it is based;

Subsection.Text: Subsection 360(4) of the Act is replaced by the following:

The auditor shall have access at any reasonable time to all of the third party's documents that, in the auditor's opinion, are necessary to enable the auditor to prepare the report, and may require the third party to provide any information or explanation that, in the auditor's opinion, is necessary to enable the auditor to prepare the report.

The auditor shall have access at any reasonable time to all of the documents of the third party, and may require the third party to provide any information or explanation, that, in the auditor's opinion, is necessary to enable the auditor to prepare the report.

Section.Text: Section 361 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer may correct a third-party expenses return filed under subsection 359(1) if the correction does not materially affect its substance.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Corrections or revisions at request of Chief Electoral Officer
Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer may in writing request a third party to correct or revise, within a specified period, a third-party expenses return filed under subsection 359(1).
If the Chief Electoral Officer requests a correction or revision, the third party shall provide him or her with the corrected or revised version of the return within the specified period.

The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written application of a third party, shall authorize the extension of the period referred to in subsection 359(1) unless he or she is satisfied that the third party's failure to file the third-party expenses return under that subsection was deliberate or was the result of the third party's failure to exercise due diligence.
The application may be made within the period referred to in subsection 359(1) or within two weeks after the end of that period.

Section.MarginalNote: Corrections or revisions — Chief Electoral Officer

Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written application of a third party, shall authorize the correction or revision of a third-party expenses return filed under subsection 359(1) if he or she is satisfied by the evidence submitted by the third party that the correction or revision is necessary in order for the requirements of this Act to be complied with.
The application shall be made immediately after the third party becomes aware of the need for correction or revision.

The third party shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the corrected or revised version of the return within 30 days after the day on which the correction or revision is authorized or within any extension of that period authorized under subsection (4) or (5).

The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written application of the third party made within two weeks after the end of the 30-day period referred to in subsection (3), shall authorize the extension of that period, unless he or she is satisfied that the third party's failure to provide the corrected or revised version of the return was deliberate or was the result of the third party's failure to exercise due diligence.

The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written application of the third party made within two weeks after the end of an extension authorized under subsection (4) or under this subsection, shall authorize the further extension of that period, unless he or she is satisfied that the third party's failure to provide the corrected or revised version of the return was deliberate or was the result of the third party's failure to exercise due diligence.
A third party may apply to a judge for an order

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: relieving the third party from the obligation to comply with a request referred to in subsection 361(2);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: authorizing an extension referred to in subsection 361.1(1); or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: authorizing a correction or revision referred to in subsection 361.2(1).

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: The third party shall notify the Chief Electoral Officer that the application has been made.

Subsection.Text: The application may be made

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: under paragraph (1)(a), within the specified period referred to in subsection 361(2) or within the two weeks after the end of that period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: under paragraph (1)(b), within two weeks after, as the case may be,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: if an application for an extension is not made to the Chief Electoral Officer within the period referred to in subsection 361.1(2), the end of the two-week period referred to in that subsection,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the rejection of an application for an extension made in accordance with section 361.1, or

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: the end of the extended period referred to in subsection 361.1(1); or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: under paragraph (1)(c), within two weeks after the rejection of an application for a correction or revision made in accordance with section 361.2.

Subsection.Text: The judge shall grant an order authorizing an extension unless the judge is satisfied that the third party's failure to file the required third-party expenses return was deliberate or was the result of the third party's failure to exercise due diligence.

The judge shall grant an order authorizing a correction or revision if the judge is satisfied by the evidence submitted by the third party that the correction or revision is necessary in order for the requirements of this Act to be complied with.
The order may require that the third party satisfy any condition that the judge considers necessary for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

Section.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer may make a correction in a report referred to in subsection 359(1) if the error does not materially affect the substance of the report.
Section 362 of the Act is amended by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (a) and by replacing paragraph (b) with the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: publish, as soon as feasible, returns filed under subsection 349.91(1) or 349.92(1);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: publish, within one year after the issue of the writ, returns filed under subsection 359(1); and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: publish, as soon as feasible, a corrected or revised version of a return filed under subsection 359(1) and published under paragraph (b).

Section.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer shall, in the manner he or she considers appropriate,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: publish, within one year after the issue of the writ, reports made under subsection 359(1).

Subsection.Text: Section 364 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (1):

Subsection.MarginalNote: Exclusion — litigation expenses and personal expenses
Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this Act, any money that is used out of a nomination contestant's, candidate's or leadership contestant's own funds to pay a litigation expense or personal expense is not a contribution if it has not been deposited into the bank account referred to in

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: subsection 476.65(1), in the case of a nomination contestant;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: subsection 477.46(1), in the case of a candidate; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: subsection 478.72(1), in the case of a leadership contestant.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 364(8) of the Act is replaced by the following:

If an individual pays fees — or fees are paid on their behalf — to attend an annual or biennial convention or leadership convention of a particular registered party, the amount of the monetary contribution received by the party is the difference between the amount of the fees and the fair market value of what the fees entitle the individual to obtain.
For the purpose of subsection (8), the following are to be included in calculating what an individual is entitled to obtain:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the cost of any goods or services received by the individual personally, such as meals and promotional products; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: their share of any general expenses incurred by the registered party in holding the convention, such as expenses incurred for the rental of a meeting place or for any audiovisual equipment used.

Subsection.Text: No person or entity other than an individual who is a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act shall pay fees to attend an annual or biennial convention or leadership convention of a particular registered party, or pay fees on behalf of another individual for them to attend such a convention.

For greater certainty, the payment by or on behalf of an individual of fees to attend an annual or biennial convention or leadership convention of a particular registered party is a contribution to that party.

Section.Text: Subsection 367(7) of the Act is amended by adding the following after paragraph (b):

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: For greater certainty, contributions made by a candidate under subsection (1) to a registered party or a registered association that later transfers funds to the candidate for the purpose of their campaign do not have the effect of reducing the amount that the candidate may contribute under this subsection.

Subsection.Text: The following contributions are permitted:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: contributions that do not exceed $5,000 in total by a candidate for a particular election out of their own funds to their own campaign; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: contributions that do not exceed $25,000 in total by a leadership contestant in a particular leadership contest out of their own funds to their own campaign.

Section.Text: Subsection 368(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: No person who is permitted to accept contributions under this Act shall accept a contribution that exceeds a limit under this Act.
No person who is permitted to accept contributions under this Act shall knowingly accept a contribution that exceeds a limit under this Act.

Section.Text: Section 372 of the Act is replaced by the following:

If a registered party, a registered association, a nomination contestant, a candidate or a leadership contestant receives a contribution made in contravention of subsection 367(1) or (6) or 368(4) or section 370 or 371, the chief agent of the registered party, the financial agent of the registered association, the official agent of the candidate or the financial agent of the nomination contestant or leadership contestant, as the case may be, shall, within 30 days after becoming aware of the contravention, return the contribution unused to the contributor or, if that is not possible, pay the amount of it — or, in the case of a non-monetary contribution, an amount of money equal to its commercial value — to the Chief Electoral Officer, who shall forward that amount to the Receiver General.

If a registered party, a registered association, a nomination contestant, a candidate or a leadership contestant receives a contribution made in contravention of subsection 367(1) or 368(4) or section 370 or 371, the chief agent of the registered party, the financial agent of the registered association, the official agent of the candidate or the financial agent of the nomination contestant or leadership contestant, as the case may be, shall, within 30 days after becoming aware of the contravention, return the contribution unused to the contributor or, if that is not possible, pay the amount of it — or, in the case of a non-monetary contribution, an amount of money equal to its commercial value — to the Chief Electoral Officer, who shall forward that amount to the Receiver General.
The Act is amended by adding the following before section 375:

Subsection.Text: A nomination campaign expense of a nomination contestant is an expense reasonably incurred as an incidence of the nomination contest, including

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a nomination contest expense;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a litigation expense;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a personal expense; and

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: any fees of an auditor appointed under subsection 476.77(1) that have not been reimbursed by the Receiver General.

Subsection.Text: For greater certainty, none of the following is a nomination campaign expense:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of any administrative monetary penalty imposed under Part 19;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any amount that is required to be paid under a compliance agreement entered into under Part 19 solely as a result of that compliance agreement; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: any amount that is required to be paid under an undertaking provided under Part 19 solely as a result of that undertaking.

Subsection.Text: A nomination contest expense is any of the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: any cost incurred, or non-monetary contribution received, by a nomination contestant, to the extent that the property or service that the cost was incurred for or that was received as a non-monetary contribution is used to directly promote or oppose a nomination contestant during a nomination contest; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any acceptance by a nomination contestant of a provision of goods or services that is permitted under paragraph 364(2)(c), to the extent that the goods or services are used to directly promote or oppose a nomination contestant during a nomination contest.

Subsection.Text: Expenses for a fundraising activity, other than expenses referred to in paragraphs (3)(a) and (b) that are related to that activity, are not nomination contest expenses under subsection (1).
A nomination contest expense includes a cost incurred for, a non-monetary contribution in relation to, or a provision of goods and services in relation to,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the production of advertising or promotional material;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the distribution, broadcast or publication of such material in any media or by any other means during the nomination contest, including by the use of a capital asset;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the payment of remuneration and expenses to or on behalf of a person for their services as a financial agent or in any other capacity;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: securing a meeting space or the supply of light refreshments at meetings;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: any product or service provided by a government, a Crown corporation or any other public agency; and

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: the conduct of surveys or research during a nomination contest.

Subsection.Text: In this section, cost incurred means an expense that is incurred by a nomination contestant, whether it is paid or unpaid.

Section.Text: A litigation expense of a nomination contestant is an expense of the contestant related to an application to a judge made under this Part, including an expense related to any appeal or judicial review arising from the application.

Subsection.Text: A nomination contestant's personal expenses include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: childcare expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: expenses relating to the provision of care for a person with a physical or mental incapacity for whom the contestant normally provides such care; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a contestant who has a disability, additional expenses that are related to the disability.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Exclusions — travel and living expenses, etc.
Subsection.Text: Neither litigation expenses nor travel and living expenses are personal expenses of a nomination contestant.
Section 375 of the Act is amended by adding the following after paragraph (a):

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: a litigation expense;

Paragraph.Label: (a.2)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (a.3)
Paragraph.Text: an accessibility expense;

Section.Text: An electoral campaign expense of a candidate is an expense reasonably incurred as an incidence of the election, including

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: any fees of the candidate's auditor, and any costs incurred for a recount of votes cast in the candidate's electoral district, that have not been reimbursed by the Receiver General.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 375(c) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: any fees of an auditor appointed under subsection 477.1(2) that have not been reimbursed by the Receiver General.

Subsection.Text: Section 375 of the Act is renumbered as subsection 375(1) and is amended by adding the following:
For greater certainty, none of the following is an electoral campaign expense:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of any administrative monetary penalty imposed under Part 19;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any amount that is required to be paid under a compliance agreement entered into under Part 19 solely as a result of that compliance agreement; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: any amount that is required to be paid under an undertaking provided under Part 19 solely as a result of that undertaking.

Section.Text: Section 376 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (3):

Subsection.Text: An accessibility expense of a registered party or a candidate, as the case may be, is not an election expense of that party or candidate.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 376:
A partisan advertising expense of a registered party or an electoral district association of a registered party, as the case may be, includes any of the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: any non-monetary contribution received by the party or association, to the extent that the property or service that was received as a non-monetary contribution is used in relation to the production of a partisan advertising message or the transmission of a partisan advertising message to the public; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any acceptance by the party or association of a provision of goods or services that is permitted under subsection 364(2), to the extent that the goods or services are used in relation to the production of a partisan advertising message or the transmission of a partisan advertising message to the public.

Section.Text: Section 377 of the Act is renumbered as subsection 377(1) and is amended by adding the following:

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of subsection (1), in calculating what a ticket bearer is entitled to obtain, to be included in the calculation is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the cost of any goods or services received by the ticket bearer personally, such as meals and promotional products; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: their share of any general expenses incurred by the registered party, registered association, nomination contestant, candidate or leadership contestant, as the case may be, in holding the activity, such as expenses incurred for the rental of a meeting space or for any audiovisual equipment used.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 377:

A litigation expense of a candidate is an expense of the candidate related to any of the following requests or applications, including an expense related to any appeal or judicial review arising from the request or the application:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a request or an application made under Part 14;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: an application to a judge made under this Part; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: an application to contest the election in the candidate's electoral district.

Subsection.Text: An accessibility expense of a registered party or a candidate, as the case may be, is any of the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of any cost incurred, or non-monetary contribution received, by the party or candidate, to the extent that the property or service that the cost was incurred for — or that was received as a non-monetary contribution — is used solely to make accessible, to persons with a disability, materials used or activities held during an election period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the difference between the amounts referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii), to the extent that the amount referred to in subparagraph (i) is greater than the amount referred to in subparagraph (ii):

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount of any cost incurred, or non-monetary contribution received, by the party or candidate, to the extent that the property or service that the cost was incurred for — or that was received as a non-monetary contribution — is used for materials used or activities held during an election period and those materials or activities are accessible to persons with a disability, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount equal to the value of the property or service if the materials or activities had not been accessible to persons with a disability;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the amount equal to the value of goods or services referred to in subsection 364(2) that are accepted by the party or candidate, to the extent that the goods or services are used solely to make accessible, to persons with a disability, materials used or activities held during an election period; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the difference between the amounts referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii), to the extent that the amount referred to in subparagraph (i) is greater than the amount referred to in subparagraph (ii):

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount equal to the value of goods or services referred to in subsection 364(2) that are accepted by the party or candidate, to the extent that the goods or services are used for materials used or activities held during an election period and those materials or activities are accessible to persons with a disability, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount equal to the value of the goods or services if the materials or activities had not been accessible to persons with a disability.

Subsection.Text: An amount referred to in subsection (1) that is related to a fundraising activity, to the nomination of a person as a candidate or to the selection of a person as leader of a registered party is not an accessibility expense.
In subsection (1), cost incurred means an expense that is incurred by a registered party or a candidate, whether it is paid or unpaid.
Paragraph 378(1)(a) of the Act is repealed.
A candidate's personal expenses include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;

Subsection.Text: Subsection 378(2) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.MarginalNote: Exclusions — travel and living expenses, etc.
Subsection.Text: Neither litigation expenses nor travel and living expenses are personal expenses of a candidate.
The Chief Electoral Officer may establish categories of personal expenses and fix maximum amounts that may be incurred for expenses in each category.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 378:

Section.MarginalNote: Categories of certain expenses and maximums
Section.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer may establish, in respect of candidates, categories of personal expenses and of travel and living expenses and may fix maximum amounts of expenses that may be incurred in each category.
The Act is amended by adding the following after section 379:

Subsection.Text: A leadership campaign expense of a leadership contestant is an expense reasonably incurred as an incidence of the leadership contest, including

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a leadership contest expense;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a litigation expense;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a personal expense; and

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: any fees of an auditor appointed under Division 6 of Part 18 that have not been reimbursed by the Receiver General.

Subsection.Text: For greater certainty, none of the following is a leadership campaign expense:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of any administrative monetary penalty imposed under Part 19;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any amount that is required to be paid under a compliance agreement entered into under Part 19 solely as a result of that compliance agreement; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: any amount that is required to be paid under an undertaking provided under Part 19 solely as a result of that undertaking.

Subsection.Text: A leadership contest expense is any of the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: any cost incurred, or non-monetary contribution received, by a leadership contestant, to the extent that the property or service that the cost was incurred for or that was received as a non-monetary contribution is used to directly promote or oppose a leadership contestant during a leadership contest; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any acceptance by a leadership contestant of a provision of goods or services that is permitted under paragraph 364(2)(c), to the extent that the goods or services are used to directly promote or oppose a leadership contestant during a leadership contest.

Subsection.Text: Expenses for a fundraising activity, other than expenses referred to in paragraphs (3)(a) and (b) that are related to that activity, are not leadership contest expenses under subsection (1).
A leadership contest expense includes a cost incurred for, a non-monetary contribution in relation to, or a provision of goods and services in relation to,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the production of advertising or promotional material;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the distribution, broadcast or publication of such material in any media or by any other means during the leadership contest, including by the use of a capital asset;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the payment of remuneration and expenses to or on behalf of a person for their services as a financial agent or in any other capacity;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: securing a meeting space or the supply of light refreshments at meetings;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: any product or service provided by a government, a Crown corporation or any other public agency; and

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: the conduct of surveys or research during a leadership contest.

Subsection.Text: In this section, cost incurred means an expense that is incurred by a leadership contestant, whether it is paid or unpaid.

Section.Text: A litigation expense of a leadership contestant is an expense of the contestant related to an application to a judge made under this Part, including an expense related to any appeal or judicial review arising from the application.

Subsection.Text: A leadership contestant's personal expenses include

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: childcare expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: expenses relating to the provision of care for a person with a physical or mental incapacity for whom the contestant normally provides such care; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a contestant who has a disability, additional expenses that are related to the disability.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Exclusions — travel and living expenses, etc.
Subsection.Text: Neither litigation expenses nor travel and living expenses are personal expenses of a leadership contestant.

Section.Text: Subsection 382(3) of the Act is amended by adding the following after paragraph (a):

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: the total litigation expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (a.2)
Paragraph.Text: the total travel and living expenses that are related to travel and sojourns during the election period;

Paragraph.Label: (a.3)
Paragraph.Text: the total accessibility expenses;

Subsection.Text: As soon as feasible after receiving an electoral campaign return, any document referred to in subsection 477.59(10), (11), (12) or (15) or any corrected or revised version of those returns or documents for each candidate in an electoral district, the Chief Electoral Officer shall, in the manner that he or she considers appropriate, publish a summary report that includes the maximum election expenses allowed for the electoral district and, for each candidate,

Section.Text: Section 383 of the Act is repealed.

Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer shall, as soon as feasible after receiving the documents referred to in subsection 477.59(1) for an electoral district, deliver a copy of them to the returning officer for the electoral district.

A registered party and an eligible party shall include with the statement or report referred to in subsection (1) a statement certified by its chief agent that sets out the names of the person or persons who are authorized by the party to endorse prospective candidates at a general election.

A returning officer who receives documents under subsection (1) shall retain them for three years, or any shorter period that the Chief Electoral Officer considers appropriate, after the end of the six-month period mentioned in subsection (2).
Subsection 385(2) of the Act is amended by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (i) and by adding the following after paragraph (j):

Paragraph.Label: (k)
Paragraph.Text: the party's policy for the protection of personal information, including

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a statement indicating the types of personal information that the party collects and how it collects that information,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a statement indicating how the party protects personal information under its control,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: a statement indicating how the party uses personal information under its control and under what circumstances that personal information may be sold to any person or entity,

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: a statement indicating the training concerning the collection and use of personal information to be given to any employee of the party who could have access to personal information under the party's control,

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: a statement indicating the party's practices concerning

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the collection and use of personal information created from online activity, and

Subparagraph.Label: (vi)
Subparagraph.Text: the name and contact information of a person to whom concerns regarding the party's policy for the protection of personal information can be addressed; and

Paragraph.Label: (l)
Paragraph.Text: the address of the page — accessible to the public — on the party's Internet site where its policy for the protection of personal information is published under subsection (4).

Subsection.Text: The application for registration shall include
Section 385 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (2):
The Chief Electoral Officer may establish a maximum length for a political party's short-form name that is to be shown in election documents.
Section 385 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (3):

Subsection.MarginalNote: Publication of policy for the protection of personal information
Subsection.Text: A political party shall publish on its Internet site its policy for the protection of personal information referred to in paragraph (2)(k) before its leader applies under this section for the party to become a registered party.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 385:

Section.MarginalNote: Policy for the protection of personal information — parties already registered, etc.

Subsection.Text: Within three months after the day on which this section comes into force, the leader of a political party shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the party's policy for the protection of personal information referred to in paragraph 385(2)(k) and the Internet address referred to in paragraph 385(2)(l), if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: before the day on which this section comes into force, the leader of the party has applied under section 385 for the party to become a registered party but, as of that day, the Chief Electoral Officer has not yet informed the leader under subsection 389(1) whether or not the party is eligible for registration under section 387; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: on the day on which this section comes into force, the party is

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: an eligible party, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a registered party.

Subsection.Text: If the leader of the political party does not comply with subsection (1), then

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a party referred to in paragraph (1)(a), the party is not eligible for registration under section 387;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a party referred to in subparagraph (1)(b)(i), the party may not become a registered party under section 390; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a party referred to in subparagraph (1)(b)(ii), the Chief Electoral Officer shall implement the procedure for non-voluntary deregistration set out in sections 415, 416 and 418.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Deemed inclusion in application for registration
Subsection.Text: If the leader of a political party provides the Chief Electoral Officer with the policy and the address referred to in subsection (1) in compliance with that subsection, or in compliance with section 415, then the policy and the address are deemed, as of the day on which they are provided, to be included in the application for registration referred to in subsection 385(2) in respect of the party.

Section.Text: Section 390 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (5):

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of section 429.1 and — despite subsection (5) — sections 363 and 367, an eligible party that becomes a registered party under subsection (1) is deemed to have been registered from the first day of the pre-election period — if any — before the election period of the election referred to in that subsection.

Section.Text: Section 394 of the Act is replaced by the following:
The Chief Electoral Officer shall maintain a registry of political parties that contains the information referred to in paragraphs 385(2)(a) to (h), (k) and (l) and subsections 396(2) and 418(2).
The Chief Electoral Officer shall maintain a registry of political parties that contains the information referred to in paragraphs 385(2)(a) to (h) and subsections 396(2) and 418(2).
The Act is amended by adding the following after section 405:

Section.MarginalNote: Publication of changes to policy for the protection of personal information
Section.Text: As soon as feasible after reporting a change in its policy for the protection of personal information to the Chief Electoral Officer in writing under subsection 405(1), a registered party or an eligible party shall publish on its Internet site the updated version of the policy, incorporating the change set out in the report.
Subsection 408(5) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: No person shall make a declaration referred to in paragraph 385(2)(i) or subsection 407(2) that they know is false or misleading.
No member of a political party shall make a declaration referred to in section 385 or 407 that they know is false or misleading.

Section.Text: Section 412 of the Act is renumbered as subsection (1) and is amended by adding the following:

Subsection.MarginalNote: Deregistration — failure to publish updated policy for the protection of personal information
Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer may deregister a registered party if the party fails to publish an updated version of its policy for the protection of personal information on its Internet site in accordance with section 405.1.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Deregistration — failure to continue to have policy for the protection of personal information
Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer may deregister a registered party if the party fails to continue to have a policy for the protection of personal information referred to in paragraph 385(2)(k).

Section.Text: Section 426 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (2):

Subsection.MarginalNote: Expenses incurred by registered agent other than chief agent
Subsection.Text: Despite subsection (2), a registered agent — other than the chief agent — of a registered party shall, before incurring the party's expenses, obtain the written authorization of the chief agent to incur those expenses, and shall incur them only in accordance with that authorization.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 429:

Subsection.Text: The maximum amount that is allowed for partisan advertising expenses of a registered party for a pre-election period is $1,100,000.
The amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor referred to in section 384 that is in effect on the first day of the pre-election period.

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — partisan advertising expenses more than maximum amount

Subsection.Text: No chief agent of a registered party shall incur partisan advertising expenses on the party's behalf of a total amount of more than the maximum amount calculated under section 429.1.

No registered party shall circumvent, or attempt to circumvent, that maximum amount in any manner, including by acting in collusion with a potential candidate for the purpose of his or her engaging in partisan advertising so that the combined total of the following exceeds the maximum amount:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the potential candidate's partisan advertising expenses that relate to the partisan advertising engaged in in collusion with the party; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the party's partisan advertising expenses.

Subsection.Text: No third party, within the meaning of paragraph (a) of the definition third party in section 349, shall act in collusion with a registered party for the purpose of the registered party's circumventing that maximum amount.

Section.Text: A registered party, or a person acting on its behalf, that causes partisan advertising to be conducted shall mention in or on the partisan advertising message that its transmission was authorized by one of the party's registered agents.
Subsection 430(2) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.MarginalNote: Maximum expenses: postponement of polling day
Subsection.Text: If the Governor in Council orders the postponement of an election under subsection 59(4) for one or more electoral districts, along with the corresponding extension of the election period, then the maximum amount calculated under subsection (1) for a registered party that has endorsed a candidate in that or any of those electoral districts is increased by adding to it the product of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: $0.735 multiplied by the number of names on the preliminary list of electors in the electoral districts governed by the order in which the party has endorsed a candidate, or the number of names on the revised list of electors in those electoral districts, whichever is greater, and divided by the number of days in the election period before it was extended;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the inflation adjustment factor published by the Chief Electoral Officer under section 384 that is in effect on the date of the issue of the writ or writs for the election; and
the number of days by which the election period is extended.

Subsection.Text: If an election period is longer than 37 days, then the maximum amount calculated under subsection (1) is increased by adding to it the product of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: one thirty-seventh of the maximum amount calculated under subsection (1), and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the number of days in the election period minus 37.

Section.Text: Subsection 431(2) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: No registered party and no third party, within the meaning of paragraph (b) of the definition third party in section 349, shall act in collusion with each other for the purpose of the registered party's circumventing the maximum amount referred to in subsection (1).
No registered party and no third party, as defined in section 349, shall act in collusion with each other for the purpose of circumventing the maximum amount referred to in subsection (1).

Section.Text: Subparagraphs 432(2)(j)(i) and (ii) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: as an election expense, each of

Clause.Text: the expenses incurred by the registered party — other than accessibility expenses — whether paid or unpaid, including a statement of expenses incurred for voter contact calling services as defined in section 348.01, provided by a calling service provider as defined in that section, that indicates the name of that provider and the amount of those expenses, and
the non-monetary contributions used by the registered party as an election expense, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the accessibility expenses incurred by the registered party;

Subsection.Text: A financial transactions return shall set out

Paragraph.Label: (j)
Paragraph.Text: a return for election expenses incurred for each by-election during the fiscal period that sets out

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a statement of expenses incurred by the registered party, whether paid or unpaid, including a statement of expenses incurred for voter contact calling services as defined in section 348.01, provided by a calling service provider as defined in that section, that indicates the name of that provider and the amount of those expenses, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: a statement of non-monetary contributions used by it;

Section.Text: Subsection 433(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: If a registered party's candidates for the most recent general election received at that election at least 2% of the number of valid votes cast, or at least 5% of the number of valid votes cast in the electoral districts in which the registered party endorsed a candidate, the registered party's chief agent shall, for each quarter — in respect of a fiscal period of the registered party — that follows that general election, beginning with the quarter that immediately follows that general election and ending with the quarter in which the next general election is held, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a return that includes the information required under paragraphs 432(2)(a) to (d), (i) and (l).

If a registered party's candidates for the most recent general election received at that election at least 2% of the number of valid votes cast, or at least 5% of the number of valid votes cast in the electoral districts in which the registered party endorsed a candidate, the registered party's chief agent shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a return, for each quarter of the fiscal period of the registered party, that includes the information required under paragraphs 432(2)(a) to (d), (i) and (l).

Section.Text: The heading before section 437 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: The portion of subsection 437(2) of the English version of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:
An election expenses return shall set out
An election expenses return shall set out as an election expense each of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the expenses incurred by the registered party, whether paid or unpaid, including a statement of expenses incurred for voter contact calling services as defined in section 348.01, provided by a calling service provider as defined in that section, that indicates the name of that provider and the amount of those expenses; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the non-monetary contributions used by the registered party as an election expense.

Subsection.Text: Paragraphs 437(2)(a) and (b) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: as an election expense, each of

Subparagraph.Text: the expenses incurred by the registered party — other than accessibility expenses — whether paid or unpaid, including a statement of expenses incurred for voter contact calling services as defined in section 348.01, provided by a calling service provider as defined in that section, that indicates the name of that provider and the amount of those expenses, and
the non-monetary contributions used by the registered party as an election expense;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the accessibility expenses incurred by the registered party; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a general election held on a day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2, the partisan advertising expenses incurred by the registered party in relation to partisan advertising messages transmitted during the pre-election period.

Subsection.Text: Section 437 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (2):

The Chief Electoral Officer may require the chief agent to provide by a specified date documents evidencing any expense set out in the election expenses return, including bank statements, deposit slips and cancelled cheques.

Section.Text: The heading before section 444 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Heading.TitleText: Reimbursement of Election Expenses and Accessibility Expenses

Section.Text: The portion of subsection 444(1) of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: On receipt from a registered party of the documents referred to in subsection 437(1), the Chief Electoral Officer shall provide the Receiver General with a certificate that sets out the amount that is the sum of 50% of the registered party's election expenses, as set out in the return for its general election expenses, that were paid by its registered agents and 90% — to a maximum of $250,000 — of the registered party's accessibility expenses, as set out in that return, that were paid by its registered agents, if

On receipt from a registered party of the documents referred to in subsection 437(1), the Chief Electoral Officer shall provide the Receiver General with a certificate that sets out the amount that is 50% of the registered party's election expenses that were paid by its registered agents as set out in the return for its general election expenses if

Section.Text: Section 450 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — incurring partisan advertising expenses, etc.

Subsection.Text: No electoral district association of a registered party shall

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: incur partisan advertising expenses in relation to partisan advertising messages that promote or oppose a registered party or an eligible party and that are transmitted during a pre-election period; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: transmit or cause to be transmitted, during a pre-election period, partisan advertising messages that promote or oppose a registered party or an eligible party.

Subsection.Text: Despite paragraph (1)(a), an electoral district association of a registered party may incur partisan advertising expenses to the extent that the goods or services that the partisan advertising expense is incurred for are

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: provided to that party, if permitted under paragraph 364(2)(b); or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: sold to that party.

Subsection.Text: No electoral district association of a registered party shall incur election expenses.
For the purposes of subsection (1),

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: election expense has the meaning given to that expression by subsection 376(1), except that the reference to "a registered party or a candidate" is to be read as a reference to "an electoral district association"; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: subsections 376(2) to (4) apply, other than paragraph 376(3)(c), except that the reference to "a registered party or a candidate" in subsection 376(4) is to be read as a reference to "an electoral district association".

Subsection.Text: Despite subsection (1), an electoral district association of a registered party may incur an election expense to the extent that the property or service that the cost was incurred for or the non-monetary contribution was received for — or the goods or services that were accepted — are

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: provided to that party, a registered association of that party or a candidate endorsed by that party, if permitted under paragraph 364(2)(b); or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: sold to that party or a candidate endorsed by that party.

Subsection.Text: In the case of a general election that is not held on a day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2, or of a by-election, an electoral district association is deemed not to have incurred an election expense for election advertising if, on the issue of the writ or writs, it is not able to cancel the transmission of the election advertising message that the expense is in relation to.
No electoral district association of a registered party shall, during an election period, incur expenses for — or transmit or cause to be transmitted — election advertising as defined in section 319.

If a general election is held on a date other than one set out in subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2, or if a by-election is held, an electoral district association does not incur expenses for election advertising as defined in section 319, or transmit it or cause it to be transmitted, if, on the issue of the writ or writs, the association is not able to cancel the transmission of that advertising.

Section.Text: The portion of section 464 of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:
On or before May 31 of every year a registered association shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with

On or before May 31 of every year, unless an election campaign is in progress in that electoral district on that date, in which case the date is July 31, a registered association shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with
Subsection 469(4) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: As soon as a proclamation is issued under section 25 of the Electoral Boundaries Readjustment Act relating to a representation order, an application may be made under section 448 for the registration of an electoral district association for an electoral district that is created by — or whose boundaries are revised as a result of — the order. The electoral district association may be registered at any time on or after the day on which the application is made.

As soon as a proclamation is issued under section 25 of the Electoral Boundaries Readjustment Act relating to a representation order, an application may be made under section 448 for the registration of an electoral district association for an electoral district that is created by — or whose boundaries are revised as a result of — the order. Any resulting registration does not take effect before the order comes into force.

Section.Text: Subsection 475.6(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: The auditor of a registered association that has, in a fiscal period, accepted contributions of $10,000 or more in total or incurred expenses of $10,000 or more in total shall report to the association's financial agent on the association's financial transactions return and shall, in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards, make any examination that will enable the auditor to give an opinion in the report as to whether the return presents fairly the information contained in the financial records on which it is based.

The auditor of a registered association that has, in a fiscal period, accepted contributions of $5,000 or more in total or incurred expenses of $5,000 or more in total shall report to the association's financial agent on the association's financial transactions return and shall, in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards, make any examination that will enable the auditor to give an opinion in the report as to whether the return presents fairly the information contained in the financial records on which it is based.

Section.Text: Section 475.8 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (2):

Subsection.Text: The $1,500 amount set out in subsection (1) shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor referred to in section 384 that is in effect on the last day of the registered association's fiscal period to which the auditor's report relates.

Section.Text: The heading before section 476 of the French version of the Act is replaced by the following:
Section 476 of the Act is replaced by the following:
In this Division, selection date means the date on which a nomination contest is decided. (date de désignation)
The following definitions apply in this Division.

Definition.Text: personal expenses means the expenses of a personal nature that are reasonably incurred by or on behalf of a nomination contestant in relation to their nomination campaign and includes

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: childcare expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: expenses relating to the provision of care for a person with a physical or mental incapacity for whom the contestant normally provides such care; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a contestant who has a disability, additional expenses that are related to the disability. (dépense personnelle)

Definition.Text: selection date means the date on which a nomination contest is decided. (date de désignation)

Section.Text: Subsection 476.65(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: All of a nomination contestant's financial transactions in relation to the contestant's nomination campaign that involve the receipt of money are to be deposited to the account unless the transaction involves the receipt of the contestant's own funds and those funds are used to pay a litigation expense or a personal expense.

All of a nomination contestant's financial transactions in relation to the contestant's nomination campaign that involve the payment of money are to be paid from the account unless the transaction involves the payment out of the contestant's own funds of a litigation expense or a personal expense.

All of a nomination contestant's financial transactions in relation to the contestant's nomination campaign that involve the payment or receipt of money are to be paid from or deposited to the account.
Subsection 476.66(4) of the Act is replaced by the following:
No person or entity, other than a nomination contestant's financial agent, shall pay the contestant's nomination campaign expenses except for

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a litigation expense;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;
a personal expense; or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a petty expense referred to in section 381.

Subsection.Text: No person or entity, other than the financial agent of a nomination contestant, shall pay the contestant's nomination campaign expenses, other than personal expenses.
Subsection 476.66(6) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.MarginalNote: Prohibition — paying contestant's personal expenses, etc.
Subsection.Text: No person or entity, other than the nomination contestant or their financial agent, shall pay the contestant's expenses referred to in any of paragraphs 4(a) to (c).
No person or entity, other than the nomination contestant or their financial agent, shall pay the contestant's personal expenses.

Section.Text: The portion of section 476.67 of the Act before paragraph (b) is replaced by the following:
The limit for nomination contest expenses that is allowed for a nomination contestant in an electoral district is the amount

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that is 20% of the election expenses limit that was calculated under subsection 477.49(1) for that electoral district during the immediately preceding general election, if the boundaries for the electoral district have not changed since then; or

Section.Text: The limit for nomination campaign expenses — other than personal expenses — that is allowed for a nomination contestant in an electoral district is the amount

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that is 20% of the election expenses limit that was calculated under section 477.49 for that electoral district during the immediately preceding general election, if the boundaries for the electoral district have not changed since then; or

Section.Text: Subsection 476.68(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: No nomination contestant and no financial agent of a nomination contestant shall incur total nomination contest expenses in an amount that is more than the limit allowed for that electoral district under section 476.67.

No nomination contestant and no financial agent of a nomination contestant shall incur total nomination campaign expenses — other than personal expenses — in an amount that is more than the limit allowed for that electoral district under section 476.67.
Paragraph 476.75(2)(a) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of nomination contest expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of litigation expenses that includes an indication of which of those expenses were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 476.65(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them;

Paragraph.Label: (a.2)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of travel and living expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (a.3)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of personal expenses that includes an indication of which of those expenses were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 476.65(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them;

Paragraph.Label: (a.4)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of nomination campaign expenses, other than the expenses referred to in paragraphs (a) to (a.3);

Subsection.Text: The nomination campaign return shall set out

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of nomination campaign expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of the commercial value of goods or services provided and of funds transferred by the nomination contestant to a registered party, a registered association, or a candidate;

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 476.75(2)(h) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of the funds transferred by the nomination contestant to a registered party, a registered association or a candidate;

Subsection.Text: Subsection 476.75(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Together with the nomination campaign return, the nomination contestant's financial agent shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with documents evidencing expenses set out in the return, including bank statements, deposit slips, cancelled cheques and the contestant's written statement referred to in subsection 476.82(1).

Together with the nomination campaign return, the nomination contestant's financial agent shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with documents evidencing expenses set out in the return, including bank statements, deposit slips, cancelled cheques and the contestant's written statement concerning personal expenses referred to in subsection 476.82(1).
Subsection 476.75(9) of the Act is amended by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (a), by adding "and" at the end of paragraph (b) and by adding the following after paragraph (b):

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the Chief Electoral Officer is deemed to have received the declaration for the purpose of section 476.901.

Subsection.Text: If a nomination contestant dies without having sent the declaration within the period referred to in subsection (8),
Paragraphs 476.82(1)(a) and (b) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sets out the following:

Subparagraph.Text: the amount of any travel and living expenses paid by the contestant and details of those expenses, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount of any litigation expenses and personal expenses paid by the contestant, details of those expenses and an indication of which of them were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 476.65(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: declares that the contestant did not pay for any travel and living expenses, litigation expenses or personal expenses.

Subsection.Text: A nomination contestant shall, within three months after the selection date, send their financial agent a written statement in the prescribed form that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sets out the amount of any personal expenses that the contestant paid and details of those personal expenses, including documentation of their payment; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: declares that the contestant did not pay for any personal expenses.

Subsection.Text: Section 476.82 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (1):
Together with the statement referred to in paragraph (1)(a), the nomination contestant shall send their financial agent documents evidencing the payment of the expenses referred to in the statement.
Section 476.82 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (2):

If, after having sent their financial agent the statement referred to in subsection (1), a nomination contestant pays a litigation expense other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 476.65(1), the contestant shall, as soon as feasible after paying it,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: notify their financial agent of the payment;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: inform their financial agent of the amount of the expense, the details of the expense and the source of the funds used to pay it; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: send their financial agent documents evidencing payment of the expense.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 476.89:
No nomination contestant shall send to their financial agent a declaration referred to in paragraph 476.75(1)(d) that they know or reasonably ought to know is false or misleading.
Section 476.9 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — false, misleading or incomplete document
Section.Text: No financial agent of a nomination contestant shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a document referred to in subsection 476.75(1), (10), (11), (12) or (15) that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the financial agent knows or ought reasonably to know contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a document referred to in paragraph 476.75(1)(a), does not substantially set out the information required under subsection 476.75(2) and, in the case of a document referred to in subsection 476.75(10), (11), (12) or (15), does not substantially set out the information required under that subsection.
