Subsection.Text: On receipt of the documents referred to in subsection 476.75(1), including the auditor's report, and a copy of the auditor's invoice for the report, the Chief Electoral Officer shall provide the Receiver General with a certificate that sets out the greater of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of the expenses incurred for the audit, up to a maximum of the lesser of 3% of the nomination contestant's nomination contest expenses and $1,500, and

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the certificate, the Receiver General shall pay the amount set out in it to the auditor out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

The $1,500 amount set out in paragraph (1)(a) and the $250 amount set out in paragraph (1)(b) shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor referred to in section 384 that is in effect on the selection date.

Section.Text: No nomination contestant and no financial agent of a nomination contestant shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a document referred to in subsection 476.75(1), (10), (11), (12) or (15) that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the contestant or the financial agent, as the case may be, knows or ought reasonably to know contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a document referred to in subsection 476.75(1), does not substantially set out the information required under subsection 476.75(2) and, in the case of a document referred to in subsection 476.75(10), (11), (12) or (15), does not substantially set out the information required under that subsection.

Section.Text: Section 476.91 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: The surplus amount of nomination campaign funds that a nomination contestant receives for a nomination contest is the amount by which the sum of the following is more than the sum of the contestant's nomination campaign expenses paid from the bank account referred to in subsection 476.65(1) and any transfers referred to in paragraph 364(5)(a):

Paragraph.Text: contributions accepted by the financial agent on behalf of the contestant;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: money received from the sale referred to in subsection (2); and
any other amounts received by the contestant for their nomination campaign that are required to be deposited into the bank account referred to in subsection 476.65(1) and are not repayable.

Subsection.Text: Before the surplus amount of nomination campaign funds is disposed of in accordance with sections 476.92 and 476.93, a nomination contestant's financial agent shall sell, at their fair market value, any capital assets whose acquisition constitutes a nomination campaign expense.

Section.Text: The surplus amount of nomination campaign funds that a nomination contestant receives for a nomination contest is the amount by which the contributions accepted by the financial agent on behalf of the contestant and any other amounts received by the contestant for their nomination campaign that are not repayable are more than the contestant's nomination campaign expenses paid under this Act and any transfers referred to in paragraph 364(5)(a).
Section 477 of the Act is replaced by the following:

For the purposes of Division 1 of this Part and this Division, except sections 477.89 to 477.95, a candidate is deemed to have been a candidate from the time they accept a provision of goods or services under section 364, accept a transfer of funds under that section, accept a contribution, borrow money under section 373 or incur an electoral campaign expense within the meaning of subsection 375(1).

For the purposes of Division 1 of this Part and this Division, except sections 477.89 to 477.95, a candidate is deemed to have been a candidate from the time they accept a provision of goods or services under section 364, accept a transfer of funds under that section, accept a contribution, borrow money under section 373 or incur an electoral campaign expense referred to in section 375.
Section 477.1 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: A candidate shall appoint an official agent before accepting a provision of goods or services under section 364, accepting a transfer of funds under that section, accepting a contribution, borrowing money under section 373 or incurring an electoral campaign expense within the meaning of subsection 375(1).
A candidate shall appoint an auditor without delay if

Text.Ins: they accept contributions of $10,000 or more in total;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: they incur electoral campaign expenses of $10,000 or more in total; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: they receive 10% or more of the valid votes cast in the electoral district in which they are a candidate.

Subsection.Text: A candidate shall appoint an official agent before accepting a provision of goods or services under section 364, accepting a transfer of funds under that section, accepting a contribution, borrowing money under section 373 or incurring an electoral campaign expense referred to in section 375.
A candidate shall appoint an auditor on appointing an official agent.

Section.Text: Subsection 477.46(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: All of a candidate's financial transactions in relation to the candidate's electoral campaign that involve the receipt of money are to be deposited to the account unless the transaction involves the receipt of the candidate's own funds and those funds are used to pay a litigation expense or a personal expense.

All of a candidate's financial transactions in relation to the candidate's electoral campaign that involve the payment of money are to be paid from the account unless the transaction involves the payment out of the candidate's own funds of a litigation expense or a personal expense.
All of a candidate's financial transactions in relation to the candidate's electoral campaign that involve the payment or receipt of money are to be paid from or deposited to the account.
Subsection 477.47(4) of the Act is replaced by the following:
No person or entity, other than a candidate's official agent, shall pay the candidate's electoral campaign expenses except for

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a litigation expense;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;
a personal expense; or
a petty expense referred to in section 381.

Subsection.Text: No person or entity, other than the candidate's official agent, shall pay expenses in relation to a candidate's electoral campaign except for petty expenses referred to in section 381 and the candidate's personal expenses.
Subsection 477.47(6) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Despite subsection (5), a candidate shall, before incurring election expenses, obtain the written authorization of their official agent to incur those expenses, and shall incur them only in accordance with that authorization.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Prohibition — paying candidate's personal expenses, etc.
Subsection.Text: No person or entity, other than a candidate or their official agent, shall pay the candidate's expenses referred to in any of paragraphs (4)(a) to (c).
No person or entity, other than a candidate or their official agent, shall pay the candidate's personal expenses.

Section.Text: Section 477.48 of the Act and the heading before it are repealed.

ExplanatoryNote.Label: Clause 291:
ExplanatoryNote.ExplanatoryText: Existing text of the heading and section 477.48:

Heading.TitleText: Expense Limit for Notices of Nomination Meetings

Subsection.Text: The amount that may be spent on providing notice of meetings that are to be held during an election period for the principal purpose of nominating a candidate for an election in an electoral district shall not be more than 1% of the maximum election expenses

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that were allowed for a candidate in that electoral district during the immediately preceding general election, if the boundaries for the electoral district have not changed since then; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: that the Chief Electoral Officer determines, in any other case.

Subsection.Text: No candidate, official agent of a candidate or person who is authorized under paragraph 477.55(c) to enter into contracts shall incur or cause to be incurred total expenses on account of notices referred to in subsection (1) in an amount that is more than the amount determined under that subsection.

Section.Text: Subsection 477.49(2) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.MarginalNote: Maximum expenses: postponement of polling day
Subsection.Text: If the Governor in Council orders the postponement of polling day under subsection 59(4) for an electoral district along with the corresponding extension of the election period, then the election expenses limit calculated under subsection (1) for a candidate in that electoral district is increased by adding to it the product of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the election expenses limit calculated under subsection (1) divided by the number of days in the election period before it was extended, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the number of days by which the election period is extended.

Subsection.Text: If an election period is longer than 37 days, then the election expenses limit calculated under subsection (1) is increased by adding to it the product of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: one thirty-seventh of the election expenses limit calculated under subsection (1), and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the number of days in the election period minus 37.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 477.55:

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — entering into contracts without authorization
Section.Text: No person authorized under paragraph 477.55(c) to enter into contracts shall enter into any contract in relation to an electoral campaign other than a contract that they are authorized in writing by the official agent to enter into under that paragraph.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 477.59(1)(b) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the appointment of an auditor is required under subsection 477.1(2), the auditor's report on the return under section 477.62;

Subsection.Text: A candidate's official agent shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the following in respect of an election:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the auditor's report on the return under section 477.62;

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 477.59(2)(b) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of litigation expenses that includes an indication of which of those expenses were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them;

Paragraph.Label: (a.2)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of travel and living expenses that includes an indication of which of those expenses relate to travel and sojourns during the election period;

Paragraph.Label: (a.3)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of accessibility expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (a.4)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of personal expenses that includes

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: an indication of which of those expenses are childcare expenses,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: an indication of which of those expenses are expenses referred to in paragraphs 378(1)(c) and (d), and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: an indication of which of those expenses were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of electoral campaign expenses, other than the expenses referred to in paragraphs (a) to (a.4), including a statement of electoral campaign expenses incurred for voter contact calling services as defined in section 348.01, provided by a calling service provider as defined in that section, that indicates the name of that provider and the amount of those expenses;

Subsection.Text: The electoral campaign return shall set out

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of electoral campaign expenses, other than election expenses, including a statement of electoral campaign expenses incurred for voter contact calling services as defined in section 348.01, provided by a calling service provider as defined in that section, that indicates the name of that provider and the amount of those expenses;

Subsection.Text: Subsection 477.59(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Together with the electoral campaign return, the official agent of a candidate shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with documents evidencing expenses set out in the return, including bank statements, deposit slips, cancelled cheques and the candidate's written statement referred to in subsection 477.64(1).

Together with the electoral campaign return, the official agent of a candidate shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with documents evidencing expenses set out in the return, including bank statements, deposit slips, cancelled cheques and the candidate's written statement concerning personal expenses referred to in subsection 477.64(1).
Paragraphs 477.64(1)(a) and (b) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sets out the following:

Subparagraph.Text: the amount of any travel and living expenses paid by the candidate and details of those expenses, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount of any litigation expenses and personal expenses paid by the candidate, details of those expenses and an indication of which of them were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: declares that the candidate did not pay for any travel and living expenses, litigation expenses or personal expenses.

Subsection.Text: A candidate shall, within three months after polling day, send their official agent a written statement in the prescribed form that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sets out the amount of any personal expenses that the candidate paid and details of those personal expenses, including documentation of their payment; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: declares that the candidate did not pay for any personal expenses.

Subsection.Text: Section 477.64 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (1):
Together with the statement referred to in paragraph (1)(a), the candidate shall send their official agent documents evidencing the payment of the expenses referred to in the statement.
Section 477.64 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (2):

If, after having sent their official agent the statement referred to in subsection (1), a candidate pays a litigation expense other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1), the candidate shall, as soon as feasible after paying it,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: notify their official agent of the payment;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: inform their official agent of the amount of the expense, the details of the expense and the source of the funds used to pay it; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: send their official agent documents evidencing payment of the expense.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 477.71:
No candidate shall send to their official agent a declaration referred to in paragraph 477.59(1)(d) that they know or ought reasonably to know is false or misleading.

Subsection.Text: Subsections 477.72(1) and (2) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — false, misleading or incomplete document

Subsection.Text: No official agent of a candidate shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a document referred to in subsection 477.59(1), (10), (11), (12) or (15) that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the official agent knows or ought reasonably to know contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a document referred to in paragraph 477.59(1)(a), does not substantially set out the information required under subsection 477.59(2) and, in the case of a document referred to in subsection 477.59(10), (11), (12) or (15), does not substantially set out the information required under that subsection.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Membership in House of Commons suspended — document not provided
Subsection.Text: If the Chief Electoral Officer determines, with respect to an elected candidate, that a document that was required to be provided under subsection 477.59(1), (10), (11), (12) or (15) was not provided within the period for providing it or within any extension to that period authorized under subsection 477.66(1), then, until the document is provided, the candidate is not entitled to continue to sit or vote as a member of the House of Commons as of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the expiry of the two-week period referred to in paragraph 477.68(2)(b), determined on the basis of whichever of its subparagraphs applies, if the candidate or their official agent does not apply to a judge for an order under paragraph 477.68(1)(b);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the candidate or their official agent applies to a judge for an order under paragraph 477.68(1)(b), and the application is rejected, the expiry of the day on which the application is finally disposed of so as to deny it; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the candidate or their official agent applies to a judge for an order under paragraph 477.68(1)(b) and the order is granted, the expiry of the period extended by the order.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Membership in House of Commons suspended — unmade correction or revision
Subsection.Text: If the Chief Electoral Officer determines, with respect to an elected candidate, that a correction or revision authorized to be made under subsection 477.67(1) was not made within 30 days after the day on which it was authorized, then, until the correction or revision is made, the candidate is not entitled to continue to sit or vote as a member of the House of Commons as of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the expiry of the two-week period referred to in subsection 477.67(4), if the candidate or their official agent does not apply to the Chief Electoral Officer for an extension under that subsection;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the candidate or their official agent applies to the Chief Electoral Officer for an extension under subsection 477.67(4) and it is authorized, the expiry of two weeks after the expiry of the authorized extension, unless the candidate or their official agent applies to the Chief Electoral Officer for a further extension under subsection 477.67(5);

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the candidate or their official agent applies to the Chief Electoral Officer for an extension under subsection 477.67(5) and it is authorized, the expiry of two weeks after the expiry of the authorized extension, unless the candidate or their official agent makes a further application to the Chief Electoral Officer for a extension under that subsection; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: if the candidate or their official agent applies to the Chief Electoral Officer for an extension under subsection 477.67(4) or (5), and the application is rejected, the expiry of the day on which the application is rejected.

Subsection.Text: No candidate and no official agent of a candidate shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a document referred to in subsection 477.59(1), (10), (11), (12) or (15) that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the candidate or the official agent, as the case may be, knows or ought reasonably to know contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a document referred to in subsection 477.59(1), does not substantially set out the information required under subsection 477.59(2) and, in the case of a document referred to in subsection 477.59(10), (11), (12) or (15), does not substantially set out the information required under that subsection.

Subsection.Text: If the Chief Electoral Officer determines, with respect to an elected candidate, that a document that was required to be provided under subsection 477.59(1), (10), (11), (12) or (15) was not provided within the period for providing it or within any extension to that period authorized under subsection 477.66(1) or paragraph 477.68(1)(b), or that a correction or revision was not made as authorized by subsection 477.67(1) within the period provided in subsection 477.67(3), then the Chief Electoral Officer shall so inform the Speaker of the House of Commons and the candidate is not entitled to continue to sit or vote as a member of the House of Commons until the document, correction or revision is provided or made, as the case may be.
Paragraph 477.72(3)(a) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the expiry of the two weeks referred to in paragraph 477.68(2)(a), if the candidate or their official agent does not apply to a judge for an order under paragraph 477.68(1)(a); or

Subsection.Text: If the Chief Electoral Officer determines, with respect to an elected candidate, that a correction or revision that was requested to be made under subsection 477.65(2) was not made within the period specified, then, until the correction or revision is made, the candidate is not entitled to continue to sit or vote as a member of the House of Commons as of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the end of the two weeks referred to in paragraph 477.68(2)(a), if the candidate or their official agent does not apply to a judge for an order under paragraph 477.68(1)(a); or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the candidate or their official agent applies to a judge for an order under paragraph 477.68(1)(a), the day on which the application is finally disposed of so as to deny it.

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 477.72(3)(b) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the candidate or their official agent applies to a judge for an order under paragraph 477.68(1)(a), the expiry of the day on which the application is finally disposed of so as to deny it.

Subsection.Text: Subsection 477.72(4) of the Act is replaced by the following:

As soon as an elected candidate is not entitled to continue to sit or vote as a member of the House of Commons under any of subsections (2), (2.1) and (3), the Chief Electoral Officer shall so inform the Speaker of the House of Commons.

As soon as an elected candidate is not entitled to continue to sit or vote as a member of the House of Commons under subsection (3), the Chief Electoral Officer shall so inform the Speaker of the House of Commons.

Section.Text: The heading before section 477.73 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Heading.TitleText: Reimbursement of Election Expenses and Personal Expenses

Section.Text: Subsections 477.73(2) and (3) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the certificate, the Receiver General shall pay the amount set out in it out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund to the official agent of any candidate named in the certificate as partial reimbursement for the candidate's election expenses, travel and living expenses that are related to travel and sojourns during the election period, accessibility expenses and personal expenses. The payment may be made to the person designated by the official agent.
A candidate's official agent shall without delay return to the Receiver General any amount received under subsection (2) that is more than the sum of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the candidate's paid election expenses, as set out in the their electoral campaign return,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the candidate's paid travel and living expenses that are related to travel and sojourns during the election period, as set out in their electoral campaign return,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the candidate's paid personal expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return, other than childcare expenses or expenses referred to in paragraphs 378(1)(c) and (d),

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: 90% of the candidate's paid childcare expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return,

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: 90% of the candidate's paid expenses referred to in paragraphs 378(1)(c) and (d), as set out in their electoral campaign return, and

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: 90% — to a maximum of $5,000 — of the candidate's paid accessibility expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return.

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the certificate, the Receiver General shall pay the amount set out in it out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund to the official agent of any candidate named in the certificate as partial reimbursement for the candidate's election expenses and personal expenses. The payment may be made to the person designated by the official agent.
A candidate's official agent shall without delay return to the Receiver General any amount received under subsection (2) that is more than 60% of the total of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the candidate's personal expenses that the candidate has paid, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the candidate's election expenses, as set out in the candidate's electoral campaign return.

Subsection.Text: Paragraphs 477.74(1)(c) and (d) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: states that the amount received as partial reimbursement under subsection 477.73(2) is less than the sum of the amounts calculated under paragraphs (2)(a) to (f); and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: sets out the amount of the final instalment of the reimbursement of the candidate's expenses, calculated under subsection (2).

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the documents referred to in subsection 477.59(1), or a corrected or revised version of any of those documents, in respect of a candidate named in a certificate, the Chief Electoral Officer shall provide the Receiver General with a certificate that

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: states that the candidate has incurred more than 30% of the election expenses limit calculated under section 477.49; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: sets out the amount of the final instalment of the candidate's election expenses and personal expenses reimbursement, calculated under subsection (2).

Subsection.Text: Subsection 477.74(2) of the Act is replaced by the following:
The amount referred to in paragraph (1)(d) is the sum of the following, less the partial reimbursement made under section 477.73:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the candidate's paid election expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the candidate's paid travel and living expenses that are related to travel and sojourns during the election period, as set out in their electoral campaign return,

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the candidate's paid personal expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return, other than childcare expenses and expenses referred to in paragraphs 378(1)(c) and (d),

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: 90% of the candidate's paid childcare expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return,

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: 90% of the candidate's paid expenses referred to in paragraphs 378(1)(c) and (d), as set out in their electoral campaign return, and

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: 90% — to a maximum of $5,000 — of the candidate's paid accessibility expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return.

Subsection.Text: The amount referred to in paragraph (1)(d) is the lesser of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the sum of the candidate's paid election expenses and paid personal expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return, less the partial reimbursement made under section 477.73, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the election expenses limit calculated under section 477.49, less the partial reimbursement made under section 477.73.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 477.74:
The official agent shall use any amount received under subsection 477.73(2), or received under both that subsection and subsection 477.74(4), to pay to the candidate the amount that is the sum of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: 60% of the candidate's personal expenses, as set out in their electoral campaign return, other than childcare expenses and expenses referred to in paragraph 378(1)(c) or (d), that were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1), and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: 90% of the total of the candidate's childcare expenses and expenses referred to in paragraphs 378(1)(c) and (d), as set out in their electoral campaign return, that were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1).

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 477.76:

The $1,500 amount set out in paragraph 477.75(a) and the $250 amount set out in paragraph 477.75(b) shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor referred to in section 384 that is in effect on polling day.
Section 477.77 of the Act is repealed.

Subsection.Text: The Chief Electoral Officer shall provide the Receiver General with a certificate that lists the names of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: each candidate, including one who has withdrawn under subsection 74(1), whose official agent the Chief Electoral Officer is satisfied has provided the documents under section 477.59 and returned any unused forms referred to in section 477.86, in accordance with subsection 477.88(2); and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any candidate who has died before the closing of all the polling stations.

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the certificate, the Receiver General shall pay out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund the amount of each listed candidate's nomination deposit to their official agent. The payment may be made to the person designated by the official agent.
If there is no official agent in the case described in paragraph (1)(b), the Chief Electoral Officer may return the nomination deposit to any person that he or she considers appropriate.
Any nomination deposit that is not returned under this section is forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

Section.Text: Paragraph 477.79(a) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the election is deemed to have been held on the day on which the writ is withdrawn or deemed to be withdrawn; and

Section.Text: Division 1 of this Part and this Division apply to electoral campaign expenses of candidates in an electoral district in which a writ is withdrawn under subsection 59(1) or deemed to be withdrawn under subsection 31(3) of the Parliament of Canada Act, except that in such a case

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the election is deemed to have been held on a polling day that is the day of publication of the notice of withdrawal in the Canada Gazette under subsection 59(2) or section 551; and

Subsection.Text: Subsections 477.8(1) and (2) of the Act are replaced by the following:

The surplus amount of electoral funds that a candidate receives for an election is the amount by which the candidate's electoral revenues referred to in subsection (3) are more than the total of the candidate's electoral campaign expenses paid from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1) and the transfers referred to in subsection (4).

Subsection.MarginalNote: Transfer or sale of capital assets
Subsection.Text: Before the surplus amount of electoral funds is disposed of in accordance with sections 477.81 and 477.82, a candidate's official agent shall either transfer any capital assets whose acquisition constitutes an electoral campaign expense within the meaning of subsection 375(1) to the registered party that has endorsed the candidate — or to the registered association of that party in the candidate's electoral district — or sell them at their fair market value.

The surplus amount of electoral funds that a candidate receives for an election is the amount by which the candidate's electoral revenues referred to in subsection (3) are more than the total of the candidate's electoral campaign expenses paid by their official agent and the transfers referred to in subsection (4).

Before the surplus amount of electoral funds is disposed of in accordance with sections 477.81 and 477.82, a candidate shall either transfer any capital assets whose acquisition constitutes an electoral campaign expense within the meaning of section 375 to the registered party that has endorsed the candidate — or to the registered association of that party — or sell them at their fair market value.
Paragraphs 477.8(3)(b) and (c) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any of the following for which the candidate was reimbursed under this Act:

Subparagraph.Text: an election expense,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: travel and living expenses,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: an accessibility expense,
a personal expense paid from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1), and

Text.Ins: a cost incurred in respect of a request or an application made under Part 14, if the cost was paid from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1);

Subsection.Text: The electoral revenues of a candidate include any amount that represents

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: an election expense or personal expense for which the candidate was reimbursed under this Act;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the candidate's nomination deposit for which they were reimbursed

Subsection.Text: Section 477.8 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (3):
Despite subsection (3), for the purposes of this Act, none of the following is electoral revenue:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: any amount used to pay for a candidate's litigation expenses that was not deposited into the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any amount used to pay for a candidate's personal expenses that was not deposited into the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1);

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: any amount paid to the candidate under this Act as a reimbursement of personal expenses that were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1); and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: any amount paid to the candidate under this Act as a reimbursement of a cost incurred in respect of a request or an application made under Part 14, if that cost was paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1).

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 477.8(4)(b) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any amount of a reimbursement referred to in paragraph (3)(b) that the candidate transfers to that registered party; and

Subsection.Text: A transfer made by a candidate is a transfer of

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any amount of a reimbursement referred to in paragraphs (3)(b) and (c) that the candidate transfers to that registered party; and

Section.Text: Paragraphs 477.81(3)(a) and (b) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the day on which they receive the final instalment of the reimbursement of the candidate's expenses; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the day on which the Chief Electoral Officer is provided with the candidate's electoral campaign return, if the candidate did not receive the reimbursement mentioned in paragraph (a).

Subsection.Text: If a candidate has a surplus of electoral funds but their official agent has not received a notice of estimated surplus, the official agent shall dispose of the surplus within 60 days after, as the case may be,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the later of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the day on which they receive the final instalment of the reimbursement of the candidate's election expenses and personal expenses, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the day on which they receive the reimbursement of the candidate's nomination deposit; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the day on which the Chief Electoral Officer is provided with the candidate's electoral campaign return, if the candidate did not receive either of the reimbursements mentioned in paragraph (a).

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 477.84:

Section.MarginalNote: Persons to whom this section applies

Subsection.Text: This section applies to any person who was a candidate at an election but who was not endorsed by a registered party and whose official agent disposed of the candidate's surplus electoral funds under paragraph 477.82(b).

The official agent of a candidate who is a person referred to in subsection (1) may, for the purpose of the candidate's electoral campaign, apply to the Chief Electoral Officer for repayment of the amount of the surplus electoral funds referred to in that subsection if that candidate

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is a candidate at the general election next following the election to which the funds relate but is not endorsed by a registered party and was not a candidate at any intervening by-election;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: is a candidate at one, and only one, intervening by-election and at that by-election is not endorsed by a registered party; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: is a candidate at more than one intervening by-election and, at the first intervening by-election at which they are a candidate, is not endorsed by a registered party.

Subsection.Text: On receipt of a request for payment from the Chief Electoral Officer in relation to an application, the Receiver General shall pay the amount specified in the application to the candidate's official agent out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

Section.Text: Subsection 477.9(5) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: The candidate shall provide the statement to the Chief Electoral Officer within four months after polling day.
The candidate shall provide the statement to the Chief Electoral Officer within four months after

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: polling day; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the day on which a notice of the withdrawal or deemed withdrawal of the writ for the election is published in the Canada Gazette under subsection 59(2) or section 551.

Section.Text: Section 478 of the Act and the heading "Interpretation" before it are repealed.

ExplanatoryNote.Label: Clause 309:
ExplanatoryNote.ExplanatoryText: Existing text of the heading and section 478:

Section.Text: In this Division, personal expenses means the expenses of a personal nature that are reasonably incurred by or on behalf of a leadership contestant in relation to their leadership campaign and includes

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: childcare expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: expenses relating to the provision of care for a person with a physical or mental incapacity for whom the contestant normally provides such care; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a contestant who has a disability, additional expenses that are related to the disability.

Section.Text: Subsection 478.61(3) of the French version of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.MarginalNote: Nomination d'un agent membre d'une société
Subsection.Text: Tout membre d'une société nommée conformément à la présente loi à titre de vérificateur d'un parti enregistré peut être nommé agent du candidat à la direction.

A person may be appointed as agent for a leadership contestant even if the person is a member of a partnership that has been appointed as an auditor, in accordance with this Act, for the registered party.

Section.Text: Subsection 478.72(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: All of a leadership contestant's financial transactions in relation to the contestant's leadership campaign that involve the receipt of money are to be deposited to the account unless the transaction involves the receipt of the contestant's own funds and those funds are used to pay a litigation expense or a personal expense.

All of a leadership contestant's financial transactions in relation to the contestant's leadership campaign that involve the payment of money are to be paid from the account unless the transaction involves the payment out of the contestant's own funds of a litigation expense or a personal expense.

All of a leadership contestant's financial transactions in relation to the contestant's leadership campaign that involve the payment or receipt of money are to be paid from or deposited to the account.
Subsection 478.73(4) of the Act is replaced by the following:
No person or entity, other than a leadership campaign agent of a leadership contestant, shall pay the contestant's leadership campaign expenses except for

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a litigation expense;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: travel and living expenses;
a personal expense; or

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a petty expense referred to in section 381.

Subsection.Text: No person or entity, other than a leadership campaign agent of a leadership contestant, shall pay the contestant's leadership campaign expenses, other than personal expenses.
Subsection 478.73(6) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.MarginalNote: Prohibition — paying contestant's personal expenses, etc.
Subsection.Text: No person or entity, other than the leadership contestant or their financial agent, shall pay the contestant's expenses referred to in any of paragraphs 4(a) to (c).
No person or entity, other than the leadership contestant or their financial agent, shall pay the contestant's personal expenses.
Paragraph 478.8(2)(a) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of leadership contest expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of litigation expenses that includes an indication of which of those expenses were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 478.72(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them;

Paragraph.Label: (a.2)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of travel and living expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (a.3)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of personal expenses that includes an indication of which of those expenses were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 478.72(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them;

Paragraph.Label: (a.4)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of leadership campaign expenses, other than the expenses referred to in paragraphs (a) to (a.3);

Subsection.Text: The leadership campaign return shall set out

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of leadership campaign expenses;

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of the commercial value of goods or services provided and of funds transferred by the leadership contestant to a registered party or a registered association;

Subsection.Text: Paragraph 478.8(2)(i) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of the funds transferred by the leadership contestant to a registered party or a registered association;

Subsection.Text: Subsection 478.8(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Together with the leadership campaign return, the leadership contestant's financial agent shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with documents evidencing expenses set out in the return, including bank statements, deposit slips, cancelled cheques and the contestant's written statement referred to in subsection 478.85(1).

Together with the leadership campaign return, the leadership contestant's financial agent shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with documents evidencing expenses set out in the return, including bank statements, deposit slips, cancelled cheques and the contestant's written statement concerning personal expenses referred to in subsection 478.85(1).
Subsection 478.8(9) of the Act is amended by striking out "and" at the end of paragraph (a), by adding "and" at the end of paragraph (b) and by adding the following after paragraph (b):

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the Chief Electoral Officer is deemed to have received the declaration for the purpose of section 478.931.

Subsection.Text: If a leadership contestant dies without having sent the declaration within the period referred to in subsection (8),

Section.Text: Subsection 478.83(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: As soon as feasible after the end of a leadership contest, the auditor of a leadership contestant who has accepted contributions of $10,000 or more in total or incurred leadership campaign expenses of $10,000 or more in total shall report to the contestant's financial agent on the leadership campaign return for that contest and shall, in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards, make any examination that will enable the auditor to give an opinion in the report as to whether the return presents fairly the information contained in the financial records on which it is based.

As soon as feasible after the end of a leadership contest, the auditor of a leadership contestant who has accepted contributions of $5,000 or more in total or incurred leadership campaign expenses of $5,000 or more in total shall report to the contestant's financial agent on the leadership campaign return for that contest and shall, in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards, make any examination that will enable the auditor to give an opinion in the report as to whether the return presents fairly the information contained in the financial records on which it is based.
Paragraphs 478.85(1)(a) and (b) of the Act are replaced by the following:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sets out the following:

Subparagraph.Text: the amount of any travel and living expenses paid by the contestant and details of those expenses, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount of any litigation expenses and personal expenses paid by the contestant, details of those expenses and an indication of which of them were paid other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 478.72(1) and the source of the funds used to pay them; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: declares that the contestant did not pay for any travel and living expenses, litigation expenses or personal expenses.

Subsection.Text: A leadership contestant shall, within five months after the end of the leadership contest, send their financial agent a written statement in the prescribed form that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: sets out the amount of any personal expenses that the contestant paid and details of those personal expenses, including documentation of their payment; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: declares that the contestant did not pay for any personal expenses.

Subsection.Text: Section 478.85 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (1):
Together with the statement referred to in paragraph (1)(a), the leadership contestant shall send their financial agent documents evidencing the payment of the expenses referred to in the statement.
Section 478.85 of the Act is amended by adding the following after subsection (2):

If, after having sent their financial agent the statement referred to in subsection (1), a leadership contestant pays a litigation expense other than from the bank account referred to in subsection 478.72(1), the contestant shall, as soon as feasible after paying it,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: notify their financial agent of the payment;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: inform their financial agent of the amount of the expense, the details of the expense and the source of the funds used to pay it; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: send their financial agent documents evidencing payment of the expense.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 478.92:
No leadership contestant shall send to their financial agent a declaration referred to in paragraph 478.8(1)(d) that they know or ought reasonably to know is false or misleading.
Section 478.93 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Prohibition — false, misleading or incomplete document
Section.Text: No financial agent of a leadership contestant shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a document referred to in subsection 478.8(1), (10), (11), (12) or (15) that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the financial agent knows or ought reasonably to know contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a document referred to in paragraph 478.8(1)(a), does not substantially set out the information required under subsection 478.8(2) and, in the case of a document referred to in subsection 478.8(10), (11), (12) or (15), does not substantially set out the information required under that subsection.

Section.Text: No leadership contestant and no financial agent of a leadership contestant shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a document referred to in subsection 478.8(1), (10), (11), (12) or (15) that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the contestant or the financial agent, as the case may be, knows or ought reasonably to know contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a document referred to in subsection 478.8(1), does not substantially set out the information required under subsection 478.8(2) and, in the case of a document referred to in subsection 478.8(10), (11), (12) or (15), does not substantially set out the information required under that subsection.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 478.93:

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the documents referred to in subsection 478.8(1), including the auditor's report, and a copy of the auditor's invoice for the report, the Chief Electoral Officer shall provide the Receiver General with a certificate that sets out the greater of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of the expenses incurred for the audit, up to a maximum of the lesser of 3% of the leadership contestant's leadership contest expenses and $1,500, and

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the certificate, the Receiver General shall pay the amount set out in it to the auditor out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

The $1,500 amount set out in paragraph (1)(a) and the $250 amount set out in paragraph (1)(b) shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor referred to in section 384 that is in effect on the day on which the leadership contest ends.

Section.Text: Section 478.94 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: The surplus amount of leadership campaign funds that a leadership contestant receives for a leadership contest is the amount by which the sum of the following is more than the sum of the contestant's leadership campaign expenses paid from the bank account referred to in subsection 478.72(1) and any transfers referred to in paragraph 364(5)(b):

Paragraph.Text: contributions accepted by the leadership campaign agents on behalf of the contestant;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: money received from the sale referred to in subsection (2);
amounts referred to in subsection 365(3); and
any other amounts received by the contestant for their leadership campaign that are required to be deposited into the bank account referred to in subsection 478.72(1) and are not repayable.

Subsection.Text: Before the surplus amount of leadership campaign funds is disposed of in accordance with sections 478.95 and 478.96, a leadership contestant's financial agent shall sell, at their fair market value, any capital assets whose acquisition constitutes a leadership campaign expense.

Section.Text: The surplus amount of leadership campaign funds that a leadership contestant receives for a leadership contest is the amount by which the sum of contributions accepted by the leadership campaign agents on behalf of the contestant, amounts referred to in subsection 365(3) and any other amounts received by the contestant for their leadership campaign that are not repayable is more than the sum of the contestant's leadership campaign expenses paid under this Act and any transfers referred to in paragraph 364(5)(b).

Subsection.Text: Subsections 479(2) and (3) of the Act are replaced by the following:
Every election officer is responsible for maintaining order during voting hours at any place where voting takes place in accordance with Part 9 or 10.

In performing his or her duty under subsection (1) or (2), an election officer may order a person to leave the returning officer's office or other place where the vote is taking place if the person is committing — or the officer believes on reasonable grounds that the person has committed — in the office or place an offence under this Act, any other Act of Parliament or any regulation made under any other Act of Parliament that threatens the maintenance of order.

Every deputy returning officer, central poll supervisor and person appointed under paragraph 124(1)(b) is responsible for maintaining order during voting hours at any place where voting takes place in accordance with Part 9 or 10.

In performing his or her duty under subsection (1) or (2), an election officer may, if a person is committing, in the returning officer's office or other place where the vote is taking place, an offence referred to in paragraph 5(a), section 7 or paragraph 167(1)(a) or an offence under this Act or any other Act of Parliament that threatens the maintenance of order, or if the officer believes on reasonable grounds that a person has committed such an offence in such a place, order the person to leave the office or place or arrest the person without warrant.
Subsections 479(5) to (7) of the Act are replaced by the following:

If a returning officer or other election officer believes on reasonable grounds that a person has contravened paragraph 166(1)(a) or (b), the officer may cause any material that they believe on reasonable grounds was used in contravention of that paragraph to be removed from, in the case of a returning officer, his or her office or, in the case of any other election officer, the polling station.

If an order to leave an office or place is not obeyed without delay, the person who made it may use such force as is reasonably necessary to eject the person in respect of whom the order was made from the office or place.
The officer, supervisor or appointed person who arrests a person under subsection (3) shall without delay

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: advise the person of the right to be represented by counsel and give the person an opportunity to obtain counsel; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: deliver the person to a peace officer to be dealt with in accordance with the Criminal Code.

Subsection.Text: Where a returning officer, deputy returning officer, central poll supervisor or person appointed under paragraph 124(1)(b) believes on reasonable grounds that a person has contravened paragraph 166(1)(a) or (b), the officer, supervisor or appointed person may cause to be removed from, in the case of a returning officer, his or her office or, in the case of a deputy returning officer, central poll supervisor or appointed person, the polling station, any material that they believe on reasonable grounds was used in contravention of that paragraph.
Subsection 479(8) of the English version of the Act is replaced by the following:
Every election officer has, while exercising their powers or performing their duties under this section, all the protection that a peace officer has by law.
Every election officer has, while performing their duties under this section, all the protection that a peace officer has by law.

Section.Text: Subsection 480(1) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: Every person is guilty of an offence who, with the intention of delaying or obstructing the electoral process, contravenes this Act, otherwise than by committing an offence under subsection (2) or section 480.1, 481, 482 or 482.1 or contravening a provision referred to in any of sections 484 to 499.

Every person is guilty of an offence who, with the intention of delaying or obstructing the electoral process, contravenes this Act, otherwise than by committing an offence under subsection (2) or section 481 or 482 or contravening a provision referred to in any of sections 483 to 499.

Section.Text: Section 480.1 of the Act is renumbered as subsection 480.1(1) and is amended by adding the following:

Subsection.Text: A person does not commit an offence under subsection (1) if they establish that the representation was manifestly for the purpose of parody or satire.

Section.Text: Sections 481 and 482 of the Act are replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: Every person or entity is guilty of an offence that, during an election period, distributes, transmits or publishes any material, regardless of its form, that purports to be made, distributed, transmitted or published by or under the authority of a political party, candidate or prospective candidate if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the person or entity was not authorized by that political party, candidate or prospective candidate to distribute, transmit or publish it; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the person or entity distributes, transmits or publishes it with the intent of misleading the public into believing that it was made, distributed, transmitted or published by or under the authority of that political party, candidate or prospective candidate.

Subsection.Text: In determining whether a person or entity has committed an offence under subsection (1) the court may consider whether the material included the use of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a name, logo, social media account identifier, username or domain name that is distinctive and commonly associated with the political party, candidate or prospective candidate; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the name, voice, image or signature of the candidate or prospective candidate or of a public figure who is associated with the political party.

Subsection.Text: A person or entity does not commit an offence under subsection (1) if they establish that the material was manifestly distributed, transmitted or published for the purpose of parody or satire.
Every person or entity is guilty of an offence that, fraudulently, and with the intention of affecting the results of an election,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: by means of an electro-magnetic, acoustic, mechanical or other device, intercepts or causes to be intercepted, directly or indirectly, any function of a computer system;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: uses or causes to be used, directly or indirectly, a computer system with intent to

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: commit an offence under paragraph (a),

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: destroy or alter computer data,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: render computer data meaningless, useless or ineffective,

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: obstruct, interrupt or interfere with the lawful use of computer data, or

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: obstruct, interrupt or interfere with a person or entity in the lawful use of computer data or deny access to computer data to a person or entity that is entitled to access to it; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: uses, possesses or traffics in, or permits another person or entity to have access to, a computer password that would enable a person or entity to commit an offence under paragraph (a) or (b).

Subsection.Text: Words and expressions used in subsection (1) have the same meaning as in subsection 342.1(2) of the Criminal Code.

Every person is guilty of an offence who, during an election period, directly or indirectly offers a bribe to influence an elector to vote or refrain from voting or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate.
Every elector is guilty of an offence who, during an election period, accepts or agrees to accept a bribe that is offered in the circumstances described in subsection (1).

Section.Text: Every person is guilty of an offence who

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: by intimidation or duress, compels a person to vote or refrain from voting or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate at an election; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: by any pretence or contrivance, including by representing that the ballot or the manner of voting at an election is not secret, induces a person to vote or refrain from voting or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate at an election.

Section.Text: Section 503 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: A political party that is deregistered during a pre-election period does not commit an offence under paragraph 495.3(1)(a) or (2)(a) if, before the deregistration, its partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses exceeded any maximum amount set out in section 349.1.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Prior expenses applied against spending limit
Subsection.Text: If subsection (1) applies, then partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses incurred before the deregistration shall be applied against any maximum amount set out in section 349.1 and, if the limit is exceeded, the political party shall not incur any additional partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

A political party that is deregistered during an election period does not commit an offence under paragraph 496(1)(a) or (2)(a) if, before the deregistration, its partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey expenses exceeded any maximum amount set out in section 350.

An eligible party that does not become a registered party during the election period of a general election does not commit an offence under paragraph 496(1)(a) or (2)(a) if its partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey expenses, as of the day that it is informed under subsection 390(4) that it has not been registered, exceed any maximum amount set out in section 350.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Prior expenses applied against spending limit
Subsection.Text: If subsection (1.2) or (2) applies, then partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey expenses incurred before the deregistration or before the day referred to in subsection (2), as the case may be, shall be applied against any maximum amount set out in section 350 and, if the maximum amount is exceeded, the party shall not incur any additional partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

A political party that is deregistered during an election period does not commit an offence under paragraph 496(1)(a) or (2)(a) if the party, during the portion of the election period before the deregistration, has spent more than the spending limit set out in section 350.

An eligible party that does not become a registered party during the election period of a general election does not commit an offence referred to in paragraph 496(1)(a) or (2)(a) if its election advertising expenses, as of the day that it is informed under subsection 390(4) that it has not been registered, are more than the spending limit set out in section 350.

If subsection (1) or (2) applies, election advertising expenses incurred before the deregistration or before the day referred to in subsection (2), as the case may be, shall be applied against the spending limit set out in section 350 and, if the limit has been exceeded, the party shall not incur any additional election advertising expenses.

Section.Text: Section 505 of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: If a third party that is a group commits an offence under section 495.3, 496 or 496.1, the person who is responsible for the group or its financial agent commits the offence if the person or financial agent authorized, consented to or participated in the act or omission that constitutes the offence.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Prosecution of third parties — vicarious liability
Subsection.Text: For the purpose of a prosecution brought against a third party under section 495.3, 496 or 496.1, the third party is deemed to be a person and any act or omission of the person who signed the application for registration in respect of the third party — or, in the absence of an application, the person who would have signed it — or the third party's financial agent, within the scope of that person's or financial agent's authority, is deemed to be an act or omission of the third party.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Prosecution of third parties — groups or corporations ($50,000)
Subsection.Text: If a third party that is a group or corporation commits an offence under paragraph 495.3(1)(d) or 496(1)(c), the third party is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $50,000 instead of the punishment set out in subsection 500(1).

Subsection.MarginalNote: Prosecution of third parties — groups or corporations ($100,000)
Subsection.Text: If a third party that is a group or corporation commits an offence under paragraph 495.3(2)(e) or 496(2)(e), the third party is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 instead of the punishment set out in subsection 500(5).

If a third party that is a group commits an offence under section 496, the person who is responsible for the group or its financial agent commits the offence if the person or financial agent authorized, consented to or participated in the act or omission that constitutes the offence.

For the purpose of a prosecution brought against a third party under section 496, the third party is deemed to be a person and any act or omission of the person who signed an application made under subsection 353(2) in respect of the third party or, in the absence of an application, the person who would have signed it, or their financial agent, within the scope of that person's or financial agent's authority, is deemed to be an act or omission of the third party.

A third party that is a group or corporation and that commits an offence under paragraph 496(1)(c) is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $50,000 instead of the punishment set out in subsection 500(1).

A third party that is a group or corporation and that commits an offence under paragraph 496(2)(b) is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 instead of the punishment set out in subsection 500(5).

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 508:

Every person or entity that contravenes section 281.3, 281.4 or 281.5 or a provision of any of Parts 16, 17 and 18 – or that fails to comply with a requirement of the Chief Electoral Officer under any of those Parts, with a provision of a compliance agreement or with a provision of an undertaking that has been accepted by the Commissioner — commits a violation and is liable to an administrative monetary penalty in an amount established in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
A violation that is committed or continued on more than one day constitutes a separate violation in respect of each day on which it is committed or continued.

Section.MarginalNote: How act or omission may be proceeded with
Section.Text: If an act or omission may be proceeded with as a violation or as an offence under this Act, proceeding in one manner precludes proceeding in the other.
The purpose of an administrative monetary penalty is to promote compliance with this Act, and not to punish.

Subsection.Text: Subject to subsection (2), the maximum administrative monetary penalty for a violation is $1,500, in the case of an individual, and $5,000, in the case of a corporation or an entity.

The maximum administrative monetary penalty for a violation arising from the contravention of section 363 or 367 is an amount equal to twice the amount that was contributed in contravention of that section, plus

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: $1,500, in the case of an individual who contravenes section 363 or 367; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: $5,000, in the case of a corporation or an entity that contravenes section 363.

Subsection.Text: The amount of an administrative monetary penalty is to be determined taking into account

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the degree of intention or negligence on the part of the person or entity that committed the violation;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the harm done by the violation;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: whether the person or entity derived any advantage from the violation;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: whether the person or entity made reasonable efforts to mitigate or reverse the violation's effects;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: whether the person or entity has taken steps to avoid committing the violation in the future;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: whether the person or entity has provided all reasonable assistance to the Commissioner with respect to the violation, including reporting it and providing any relevant information;

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: the person's or entity's history of compliance with the provisions of this Act;

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: the person's or entity's ability to pay the penalty;

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: any aggravating and mitigating circumstances; and

Paragraph.Label: (j)
Paragraph.Text: any other factor that, in the opinion of the Commissioner, is relevant.

Subsection.Text: The Commissioner may take into account a factor under paragraph (1)(j) only if a notice that sets out the factor has been published on his or her Internet site.
Before publishing the notice, the Commissioner shall consult with the Chief Electoral Officer and then

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: consult with the Advisory Committee of Political Parties established by subsection 21.1(1); and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: publish on his or her Internet site, for the purpose of public consultation, a notice that sets out the proposed factor for at least 30 days.

Subsection.Text: Subsections 509(1) and (2) of the Act are replaced by the following:

The Commissioner of Canada Elections shall be appointed by the Chief Electoral Officer, after consultation with the Director of Public Prosecutions, to hold office during good behaviour for a non-renewable term of 10 years and may be removed by the Chief Electoral Officer for cause.
The Commissioner shall be paid the remuneration that is fixed by the Chief Electoral Officer, after consultation with the Director of Public Prosecutions.

The Commissioner of Canada Elections shall be appointed by the Director of Public Prosecutions to hold office during good behaviour for a term of seven years and may be removed by the Director of Public Prosecutions for cause.
The Director of Public Prosecutions shall not consult the Chief Electoral Officer with respect to the appointment of the Commissioner.
Subsection 509(3) of the Act is amended by adding "or" at the end of paragraph (b) and by repealing paragraphs (d) and (e).
A person is not eligible to be appointed as Commissioner if the person is or has been

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the Chief Electoral Officer, a member of his or her staff or a person whose services have been engaged under subsection 20(1); or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: an election officer referred to in any of paragraphs 22(1)(a) to (b).

Section.Text: Sections 509.1 and 509.2 of the Act are replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Position within Office of Chief Electoral Officer

Subsection.Text: The position of Commissioner of Canada Elections is within the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer.

For the purposes of sections 11 to 13 of the Financial Administration Act, the Commissioner is the deputy head in relation to the portions of the federal public administration in the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer in which the employees referred to in section 509.3 occupy their positions.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Deputy head — Public Service Employment Act
Subsection.Text: For the purposes of the Public Service Employment Act, the Commissioner is the deputy head in relation to the portions of the federal public administration in the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer in which the employees referred to in section 509.3 occupy their positions.

Section.Text: The Commissioner's duty is to ensure that this Act, other than Division 1.1 of Part 16.1, is complied with and enforced by taking any measure that is provided for in this Act, including by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: conducting investigations;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: instituting prosecutions for offences under this Act;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: entering into compliance agreements;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: issuing notices of violation that set out an administrative monetary penalty; or

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: accepting undertakings.

Subsection.Text: All decisions made and actions taken by the Commissioner under any provision of Part 19 are to be made or taken independently of the Chief Electoral Officer.
Nothing in subsection (1) precludes the Commissioner from consulting with the Chief Electoral Officer in respect of any matter if the Commissioner considers it appropriate to do so.

Section.Text: The Commissioner, if he or she considers it to be in the public interest, may take any measures, including incurring any expenses, when exercising or performing any of his or her powers, duties and functions under this Part.

The Commissioner may delegate to any member of his or her staff, subject to any restrictions or limitations that he or she may specify, any of his or her powers, duties or functions that relate to the issuance of notices of violation or the acceptance of undertakings under this Part.

Subsection.Text: The position of Commissioner of Canada Elections is within the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

For the purposes of sections 11 to 13 of the Financial Administration Act, the Commissioner is the deputy head in relation to the portions of the federal public administration in the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions in which the employees referred to in section 509.3 occupy their positions.

For the purposes of the Public Service Employment Act, the Commissioner is the deputy head in relation to the portions of the federal public administration in the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions in which the employees referred to in section 509.3 occupy their positions.

Section.Text: The Commissioner's duty is to ensure that this Act, other than Division 1.1 of Part 16.1, is complied with and enforced.
Section 509.5 of the Act is replaced by the following:

The Commissioner may authorize a person employed in the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer to assist the Commissioner in the exercise or performance of any of his or her powers, duties and functions arising from subsections 509.1(2) and (3) and in the exercise of his or her power under section 509.4, subject to the terms and conditions that the Commissioner sets.

The Commissioner may authorize a person employed in the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions to assist him or her in the exercise or performance of any of his or her powers, duties and functions arising from subsections 509.1(2) and (3) and in the exercise of his or her power under section 509.4, subject to the terms and conditions that the Commissioner sets.
The portion of section 509.6 of the Act before paragraph (a) is replaced by the following:

Section.MarginalNote: Amounts to be paid out of C.R.F.
Section.Text: The following shall be paid out of unappropriated moneys forming part of the Consolidated Revenue Fund on the certificate of the Chief Electoral Officer:
The following shall be paid out of unappropriated moneys forming part of the Consolidated Revenue Fund on the certificate of the Director of Public Prosecutions:
The heading before section 510 of the Act is replaced by the following:
Subsection 510(3) of the Act is replaced by the following:

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of Part XV of the Criminal Code, any person who is charged by the Commissioner with duties relating to the administration or enforcement of this Act is deemed to be a public officer.
The Commissioner is to conduct the investigation independently of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

Section.Text: The Act is amended by adding the following after section 510:

Section.MarginalNote: Order requiring testimony or written return

Subsection.Text: If, on application of the Commissioner or his or her authorized representative, a judge is satisfied by information on oath that there are reasonable grounds to believe that this Act has been contravened or is about to be contravened and that an individual has or is likely to have information that will provide evidence of the contravention, the judge may order the individual to

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: attend as specified in the order and be examined on oath by the Commissioner or the authorized representative on any matter that is relevant to the contravention before an individual, in sections 510.02 to 510.04 referred to as a "presiding officer", designated in the order; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: make and deliver to the Commissioner or the authorized representative, within the time specified in the order, a written return under oath showing in detail the information that is required by the order.

Subsection.Text: On receipt of the application, the judge shall fix a date for the hearing of the application and direct that notice of the hearing be given, in the manner that the judge may specify, to the individual against whom the order is sought.
No order may be made under subsection (1) against an individual who is alleged to have committed, or who is about to commit, the contravention to which the application relates.

Subsection.MarginalNote: When hearing may proceed ex parte
Subsection.Text: A judge may proceed ex parte to hear and determine the application in the absence of the individual against whom the order is sought if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the Commissioner or the authorized representative establishes to the satisfaction of the judge that the disclosure of any information set out in the application would

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
